papers.title: Read What You Hear: Reference-Free Hypotheses Evaluation with Acoustic Discrepancy (READ)
papers.venue_year: arXiv 2606.04680 (June 2026); SJTU X-LANCE — Zhihan Li, Hankun Wang, Yiwei Guo, Bohan Li, Xie Chen, Kai Yu
papers.task: Reference-free ASR hypothesis evaluation -> sentence-level N-best rescoring + segment-level system combination. THE mandatory anchor.
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam-lattice: top-5 UNIQUE hypotheses from Whisper-large-v3 beam search (beam=60, dedup). Table-3 system-combination uses a MULTI-SYSTEM pool (Whisper-large-v3, Whisper-medium, NVIDIA NeMo, Qwen2.5-Omni). NOT bare sampling, NOT +retrieval.
papers.sees_audio: YES — scorer is a frozen autoregressive TTS (CosyVoice2) that computes NLL of the speech tokens Y given text hypothesis X: READ(x,y) = -log P_theta(Y|X). Segment scores via decoder self-attention DP alignment.
papers.gold_at_train: none — off-the-shelf pretrained CosyVoice2; no ASR-model- or dataset-specific fine-tuning.
papers.gold_at_test: NO — fully reference-free (no gold transcript at test; that is the paper's thesis).
papers.training_required: None. Training-free; leverages intrinsic knowledge of the pretrained TTS.
papers.scorer_inputs: audio (speech tokens) + candidate text -> per-frame NLL 'acoustic discrepancy' map; aggregated to sentence and segment scores.
papers.selection_operator: argmin acoustic discrepancy rerank (Score = -READ) at sentence level; segment-level greedy min-READ fed as an extra candidate into ROVER token-voting.
papers.comparators: original top-1; ORACLE best-of-5 (topline); ROVER system combination; ASR internal confidence (noted overconfident); QE/eWER (needs supervision); LM rescoring (noted as text-only, no acoustic grounding).
papers.equal_budget: Fixed top-5 pool for all methods; compared against oracle over the SAME pool (equal-K vs oracle). No equal-K comparison vs a strong text-only selector (e.g. MBR).
papers.datasets_used: LibriSpeech test-clean/test-other, SPGISpeech(val), Switchboard, TEDLIUM3, VCTK-noisy, ASRU2019, TALCS (code-switch). Noise: WHAM! at SNR 0/10/20 dB.
papers.eval_protocol: WER/CER on top-5 N-best rescoring; robustness sweep at SNR 0/10/20; segment-level ROVER combination across 4 systems.
papers.failure_modes: Near-zero gains on high-quality clean data (LS-clean/other realize <20% of oracle gap); depends on a SEPARATE TTS model's coverage (not the omni model's own signal); gains concentrated under domain-shift/noise; single-task ASR only.
papers.code_available: Not confirmed in fetched text (X-LANCE typically releases; treat as unconfirmed).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: READ IS essentially our I2 for ASR. Deltas vs us: (a) pool = single-ASR beam / hand-picked multi-system, NOT our sampled omni K-pool; (b) scorer = a separate generative TTS, NOT the frozen omni decoder's OWN native signal; (c) single-task ASR, no cross-task; (d) no supply-stratification, no abstention/Goodhart. Our snr5 LibriSpeech setup mirrors its noise regime almost exactly.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: THREAT — training-free acoustic rerank beats top-1 broadly (label-free N-best selection works). I2: HARD THREAT — this is a training-free audio-grounded selector eating ~20% rel / ~half the oracle gap on 4 domain-shift ASR sets; I2 must differentiate on omni-native-signal + sampled-omni-pool + cross-task. I3: no-threat — no abstention/Goodhart/cross-task. I4: no-threat — never varies capability-supply (fixed single-beam pool).

papers.title: Re-evaluating Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding for Automatic Speech Recognition
papers.task: Label-free selection over a SAMPLED hypothesis pool via MBR (consensus / min expected risk). Canonical text-only N-best selector.
papers.candidate_source_supply: bare-model sampling: epsilon-sampling (eps=0.01, T=1.0), up to N=64 hypotheses from Whisper (small/medium/large-v3, distil-large-v3.5, Kotoba-Whisper). This is the closest supply-match to OUR sampled K-pools.
papers.sees_audio: NO — utility is TEXT-ONLY: pairwise BLEU (primary), or BLEURT / SentBERT embeddings, among candidates. No acoustic access.
papers.gold_at_train: none.
papers.training_required: None — 'does not require any additional training, easy to apply.'
papers.scorer_inputs: text-only pairwise utility among the N candidates (no audio).
papers.selection_operator: MBR: argmax_y (1/N) sum_y' u(y,y') — consensus/centroid selection.
papers.comparators: beam (B=1/5/20); ORACLE best-of-64 (topline); NoRefER (LM reranker); ProGRes (LLM+ASR-score fusion, Llama-3).
papers.equal_budget: YES — all selectors and oracle evaluated over the SAME N=64 sampled pool; ablates N and utility function. This is the equal-K discipline we want, but text-only.
papers.datasets_used: ASR: LibriSpeech, AMI-IHM, VoxPopuli, ReazonSpeech(Ja), CommonVoice(Ar/Zh/Hi/Id/Ta/Th/Vi), JSUT. ST: CoVoST2, FLEURS (En-Ja).
papers.eval_protocol: WER/CER (BLEU/chrF for ST); clean + synthetic noise SNR 0 dB; ablations over N and utility.
papers.headroom_evidence: LS clean: beam 0.042 -> MBR(N=64) 0.033, oracle 0.013 (realizes 0.009/0.029 ~= 31% of oracle gap; ~21% rel over beam). LS SNR0: 0.082 -> 0.057 (Delta 0.025, ~30% rel). ReazonSpeech CER: 0.305 -> 0.291, oracle 0.149. Reranker contrast on LS: NoRefER 0.073 (worse than beam!), ProGRes 0.043, MBR 0.033.
papers.failure_modes: Fails on AMI-IHM and very short (<6-word) utterances ('yeah','hmm','gosh') — text utility cannot discriminate; large oracle gap remains unclosed (0.033 vs 0.013); text-only => zero acoustic grounding (leaves audio headroom on the table).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: This is EXACTLY our I1 (label-free N-best selector) done text-only on sampled pools, AND is the pairwise-MBR comparator we already implemented. Our angle must be: add audio-grounding, stratify by supply, and beat MBR at equal-K. Directly reproducible on our librispeech/covost2/fleurs-r.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: HARD THREAT — MBR is the canonical label-free selector; realizes ~31% of oracle on sampled clean LS, ~30% rel under noise; a generic 'label-free N-best selector' identity is largely occupied. I2: PARTIAL/CONTRAST — text-only, so it leaves the audio-grounded headroom open (our I2 must beat MBR at equal-K). I3: no-threat — no abstention/breakpoint. I4: NEAR-MISS — ablates N and utility but NOT capability-supply (bare sampling only; no +context/+retrieval strata).

papers.title: Boosting ASR Robustness via Test-Time Reinforcement Learning with Audio-Text Semantic Rewards (ASR-TRA)
papers.venue_year: arXiv 2603.05231 (March 2026); Linghan Fang, Tianxin Xie, Li Liu
papers.task: Test-time reinforcement ADAPTATION of an ASR model using an audio-text semantic-alignment reward (label-free TTA). Closest RL cousin to our thesis.
papers.candidate_source_supply: bare-model sampling: temperature-controlled stochastic decoding + a LEARNABLE decoder prompt generate diverse transcription candidates.
papers.sees_audio: YES — reward model measures audio-text semantic alignment (specific reward model NOT named in abstract; a fetched body claim of 'CLIP' and specific WER deltas was model confabulation — DISCARD those).
papers.gold_at_train: none at test (label-free TTA); base model is pretrained.
papers.training_required: YES — UPDATES WEIGHTS at test time (both model parameters AND the decoder prompt via RL). This is NOT weight-frozen inference — it is the key contrast to our 'weight-frozen reward-guided inference-time optimization'.
papers.scorer_inputs: audio + candidate text via an audio-text semantic-alignment reward model.
papers.selection_operator: RL policy update / reward maximization over sampled candidates (adapts the decoder rather than pure selection).
papers.comparators: Test-time-adaptation baselines (pseudo-labeling, entropy minimization / SUTA-style); motivates by confirmation-bias failure of confidence-based TTA.
papers.equal_budget: Unclear from abstract.
papers.datasets_used: LibriSpeech + synthetic noise; L2-Arctic accented English.
papers.eval_protocol: WER under synthetic noise + accent; latency vs TTA baselines. NOTE: abstract gives no numbers; body WER figures from a lossy PDF fetch were unreliable — treat as unverified.
papers.headroom_evidence: Abstract: 'higher accuracy while maintaining lower latency than existing TTA baselines.' No verified oracle/headroom numbers (fetch-confabulated numbers discarded).
papers.failure_modes: Requires WEIGHT UPDATES at test time (defeats the weight-frozen requirement); reward-model identity unverified; adds test-time optimization cost/latency.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Nearest neighbor in spirit — audio-text reward over sampled ASR candidates — BUT it fine-tunes weights (test-time RL) whereas we are strictly weight-frozen selection. This paper sharply DELINEATES our niche: same reward idea, opposite weight-frozen stance.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL — does label-free candidate improvement but via weight update, not pure selection. I2: PARTIAL THREAT — audio-text reward over sampled ASR pool is conceptually adjacent to I2, but NOT weight-frozen (so it does not occupy our exact niche). I3: no-threat — no abstention/Goodhart. I4: no-threat — single noise/accent regime, no supply stratification.

papers.title: SLAM-AAC: Enhancing Audio Captioning with Paraphrasing Augmentation and CLAP-Refine
papers.task: Automated audio captioning; the CLAP-Refine step is a training-free rerank of multiple decoded candidates by CLAP audio-text similarity — the 'audio-text alignment scorer for hypothesis selection' anchor.
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam-lattice: multiple beam searches with varying beam sizes (2-8) produce candidate set B_1..B_n.
papers.sees_audio: YES — frozen CLAP: cosine similarity between input-audio embedding and candidate-caption text embedding.
papers.gold_at_train: the SLAM-AAC captioner (LLM-based) is trained; the CLAP-Refine SELECTION step itself is inference-only over a frozen CLAP.
papers.training_required: Captioner: yes. Selection step (CLAP-Refine): training-free (frozen CLAP), plug-and-play.
papers.scorer_inputs: audio + candidate caption text (frozen CLAP cosine).
papers.selection_operator: argmax CLAP audio-text cosine similarity.
papers.comparators: plain beam-search top-1. No oracle upper bound reported.
papers.equal_budget: Candidate set from multi-beam; no equal-K comparison vs a text-only selector; no oracle.
papers.datasets_used: Clotho V2, AudioCaps.
papers.eval_protocol: CIDEr, SPIDEr, SPICE, METEOR (captioning metrics — NOT verifiable WER/exact-match).
papers.headroom_evidence: AudioCaps beam -> +CLAP-Refine: CIDEr 82.7->84.1 (+1.4), SPIDEr 51.1->51.8 (+0.7), METEOR 26.1->26.8 (+0.7), SPICE 19.5->19.4 (-0.1). Modest, mostly positive; one metric regresses; no oracle gap quantified.
papers.failure_modes: Small gains and a SPICE regression; captioning has no verifiable reward (unlike our WER/exact-match); no oracle headroom reported; CLAPScore has known low human correlation (Human-CLAP finding, arXiv 2506.23553); beam pool not supply-stratified.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: The frozen-audio-text-similarity-as-selector TEMPLATE we would instantiate for I2, but on captioning (non-verifiable metrics), beam pool, no supply-stratification, no oracle. Proves the training-free audio-grounded selection MECHANISM works.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: MILD — label-free rerank works but gains tiny. I2: THREAT-TEMPLATE — demonstrates frozen audio-text-similarity selection improves outputs training-free, but on captioning not on verifiable-reward tasks; the mechanism is pre-existing, so I2's novelty must be omni-native-signal + verifiable tasks + supply/oracle framing. I3: no-threat. I4: no-threat.

papers.title: Whispering LLaMA: A Cross-Modal Generative Error Correction Framework for Speech Recognition
papers.task: Cross-modal (acoustic-grounded) generative error CORRECTION of ASR N-best: fuse Whisper acoustic encoder features into LLaMA to generate a corrected transcript.
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam-lattice / +LM: N-best from Whisper (HyPoradise-style N-best sets).
papers.sees_audio: YES — Whisper acoustic encoder features projected into the LLaMA token space alongside the N-best text.
papers.gold_at_train: YES — trains a cross-modal adapter on paired (audio, N-best, reference) data.
papers.training_required: YES — base LLaMA frozen but a cross-modal ADAPTER is trained (not training-free selection).
papers.scorer_inputs: audio (Whisper features) + N-best text -> generates a corrected hypothesis (does not just score).
papers.selection_operator: Generative correction (produces a NEW hypothesis, can go out-of-pool) — NOT reranking/selection.
papers.comparators: HyPoradise text-only GER; LM rescoring; n-best top-1.
papers.equal_budget: N/A (generation, not equal-K selection).
papers.datasets_used: HyPoradise-derived N-best sets across multiple ASR domains.
papers.eval_protocol: WER / relative WERR vs n-best.
papers.headroom_evidence: Reported ~37.66% relative WERR vs n-best (from search summary; not table-verified in fetch). Acoustic fusion beats text-only HyPoradise GER.
papers.failure_modes: Requires SUPERVISED adapter training (not training-free); generative correction can hallucinate beyond the pool (no in-pool safety); acoustic fusion adds compute.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Acoustic-grounded like our I2, but SUPERVISED and GENERATIVE (out-of-pool) vs our training-free in-pool selection. Shows acoustic info helps correction, but at the cost of training + hallucination risk that in-pool selection avoids.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: no-threat (trained, generative, not a selector). I2: CONTRAST — audio-grounded but needs training, so it does NOT occupy our training-free selection niche; it argues acoustic info is valuable (supports why I2 could work). I3: no-threat. I4: no-threat.

papers.candidate_source_supply: bare decoding pseudo-labels from an ASR model (Paraformer-based); selection is over UTTERANCES, not over an N-best hypothesis pool.
papers.sees_audio: YES — a frozen speech-text ALIGNMENT score (plus a predicted-WER estimator).
papers.gold_at_train: none for the scoring signal (reference-free).
papers.training_required: The downstream ASR is adapted (trained); the SELECTION score itself is training-free/frozen.
papers.scorer_inputs: audio + pseudo-label text -> speech-text alignment score + predicted WER (utterance-level).
papers.selection_operator: rank utterances by consistency, keep top-scoring subset, then adapt on it.
papers.comparators: random selection; reference-based (oracle) selection topline.
papers.equal_budget: selects a fixed fraction/hours of data (WER-vs-hours curves).
papers.datasets_used: Accent-adaptation sets (specific accents not extractable from PDF; Paraformer backbone).
papers.eval_protocol: WER vs hours of selected data; reference-free vs reference-based vs random.
papers.headroom_evidence: Qualitative: reference-free multimodal-consistency selection approaches reference-based selection and beats random. Exact WER numbers NOT extractable from the PDF (image tables) — flagged as unverified.

papers.title: Cycle-consistency training for end-to-end speech recognition (Hori et al.)
papers.task: Semi-supervised ASR training using an ASR->TTS->ASR cycle-consistency loss on unpaired audio. LINEAGE ANCHOR for the TTS-consistency idea (mandatory anchor: TTS-based cycle-consistency).
papers.candidate_source_supply: N/A — no inference-time candidate pool; a training loss over speech encoder states.
papers.sees_audio: YES — reconstructs the speech ENCODER STATE sequence (chosen over raw signal because the text bottleneck loses speaker traits).
papers.gold_at_train: uses paired + unpaired; the cycle loss needs no transcripts for the unpaired audio.
papers.training_required: YES — this is a TRAINING method that UPDATES ASR weights. Not an inference-time selector.
papers.scorer_inputs: speech encoder states (audio) via TTS reconstruction — used as a loss, not a per-hypothesis score.
papers.selection_operator: None — training loss, no inference-time hypothesis selection.
papers.comparators: baseline paired-only ASR model.
papers.equal_budget: N/A.
papers.datasets_used: WSJ, LibriSpeech.
papers.eval_protocol: WER.
papers.headroom_evidence: 14.7% relative WER reduction from a 100h-paired baseline by adding +360h untranscribed audio via the cycle loss.
papers.failure_modes: Training-time only (defeats training-free); needs weight updates; text bottleneck loses speaker traits (hence encoder-state cycle rather than raw-signal cycle).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: The LINEAGE ROOT of the audio-consistency idea — but born as a TRAINING loss. READ is its training-free inference-time descendant that we actually compete with. Establishes that the family's origin is supervised/weight-updating, and that the training-free selection variant is recent (2024-2026).
papers.kill_relevance: I1: no-threat. I2: no-threat (training method, not a selector). I3: no-threat. I4: no-threat. Included as the historical anchor showing audio-text-consistency began as a weight-update method, contextualizing why training-free selection (our stance) is the novel move.

families.saturation_note: The inference-time, training-free, AUDIO-GROUNDED selection niche is largely OCCUPIED for single-task ASR: READ (2606.04680) already does training-free audio-grounded N-best reranking with a frozen TTS NLL, eating ~19-21% relative / roughly half the oracle gap on 4 domain-shift ASR sets (TALCS, SWBD, TEDLIUM3, SPGI) while barely moving clean LibriSpeech; CLAP-Refine (2410.09503) proves the frozen audio-text-similarity-as-selector mechanism on captioning; and MBR (2510.19471) occupies the generic label-free N-best selector slot text-only, realizing ~31% of the oracle gap on SAMPLED (N=64) clean LibriSpeech and ~30% relative under SNR-0 noise. So a plain 'label-free N-best selector' (I1) and a 'READ-style audio rerank on ASR' (I2-for-ASR) are close to saturated. HOWEVER the entire family shares four blind spots that leave I2-on-omni-native-signals, I3, and I4 open: (a) every method FIXES the candidate pool to a single source — single-ASR beam (READ, Whispering LLaMA) or bare epsilon-sampling (MBR, ASR-TRA) — and NONE stratify by capability-supply (bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval), so I4 (supply-conditional headroom realization) is untouched; (b) the acoustic scorer is always a SEPARATE model (CosyVoice2 TTS, CLAP) or a TRAINED adapter (Whispering LLaMA, ASR-TRA weight-update, cycle-consistency), never the frozen omni decoder's OWN native likelihood/signal; (c) every method is single-task (ASR or captioning) — no cross-task selector spanning ASR/ST/SER/SLU/QA; (d) none abstain or detect a Goodhart breakpoint (I3). The one true RL cousin (ASR-TRA, 2603.05231) UPDATES weights at test time, which is exactly the stance our weight-frozen thesis rejects — it delineates rather than occupies our niche.
gaps: SUPPLY-STRATIFICATION: never studies supply-conditional pools (bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval); every method fixes ONE candidate-generation source (single-ASR beam, or bare epsilon-sampling), so oracle headroom H(c) is never decomposed by capability-supply c — the exact object of I4.

EQUAL-BUDGET vs TEXT: almost never runs an equal-K head-to-head between an audio-grounded selector and a strong text-only selector on the SAME pool. READ compares only to oracle (not to MBR at equal-K); MBR is text-only. The audio-vs-text-at-equal-K question our prototypes answer is unaddressed.

SINGLE-TASK ONLY: family is ASR (READ, MBR, Whispering LLaMA, ASR-TRA, cycle-consistency) or captioning (CLAP-Refine); NO cross-task selector across ASR/ST/SER/SLU/spoken-QA with one selection rule (I3's cross-task scope, our SLU/QA/SER datasets).
NO ABSTENTION / GOODHART DETECTION: all assume selection monotonically helps; none abstain or detect a reward-hacking breakpoint (I3 is entirely uncovered).

SCORER IS EXTERNAL / TRAINED, NEVER OMNI-NATIVE: the acoustic signal comes from a separate generative/contrastive model (CosyVoice2, CLAP) or a trained adapter / weight update (Whispering LLaMA, ASR-TRA, cycle-consistency) — never the frozen omni decoder's OWN native likelihood used as the selector (the precise gap I2 targets).

VERIFIABLE-REWARD TASKS UNDERUSED: acoustic-grounded selection is shown on WER/CER and captioning metrics, not on exact-match SLU/QA where our verifiable-reward scorers apply and where audio-grounding could matter most.

rho (FRACTION-OF-ORACLE-REALIZED) IS NOT THE HEADLINE: papers report oracle-vs-method on a fixed pool but rarely make the realized fraction rho the primary metric, and NEVER decompose rho by supply/noise — precisely our directional finding (rho_greedy ~24% snr5 / ~42% clean).

WEIGHT-FROZEN STANCE UNCLAIMED: the closest RL method (ASR-TRA) explicitly UPDATES weights at test time; no paper stakes out training-free, weight-frozen, reward-guided inference-time SELECTION over sampled omni K-pools as its identity.

papers.title: Learning to rank with BERT-based confidence models in ASR rescoring (Wu, Chen, Gandhe)
papers.task: Second-pass ASR rescoring: reorder an N-best list to lower WER (English ASR).
papers.candidate_source_supply: +LM: first-pass beam N-best that has ALREADY been re-scored by a neural LM (their LTR sits on top of an NLM-rescored system). Single fixed supply level; not stratified.
papers.sees_audio: Partial/indirect: the BERT-based confidence model ingests acoustic-derived features/scores alongside text and whole-N-best context; no raw waveform, uses the first-pass ASR's acoustic scores.
papers.gold_at_train: YES — WER-labeled data (reference transcripts) needed to build per-hypothesis quality targets for the confidence model and the LTR ranking loss.
papers.gold_at_test: NO — at inference it ranks without references.
papers.training_required: YES — supervised: train BERT confidence model + learning-to-rank (LambdaMART-style) ranker on labeled data.
papers.scorer_inputs: BERT text embedding of hypothesis + acoustic/first-pass features + N-best-list context features -> LTR score. Paper stresses 'knowledge of the entire N-best list is crucial'.
papers.selection_operator: Learning-to-rank (pairwise/listwise LTR) over the N-best; pick top-ranked. Trained ranker, not a label-free scalar.
papers.comparators: Neural-LM (NLM) rescored ASR baseline (their gains are ON TOP of NLM). No oracle-fraction or MBR reported.
papers.equal_budget: Not framed as equal-K oracle realization; fixed N-best size, WERR reported vs NLM baseline only. No equal-budget accounting of fraction-of-oracle realized.
papers.datasets_used: de-identified Alexa data; LibriSpeech test-clean & test-other.
papers.eval_protocol: Relative WER reduction (WERR) vs NLM-rescored baseline; no confidence intervals reported.
papers.headroom_evidence: Realizes +5.16% WERR on Alexa (on top of NLM), 9.38% WERR LibriSpeech test-clean, 13.63% WERR test-other. Does NOT report oracle WER or fraction (rho) of oracle headroom realized.
papers.failure_modes: Requires supervised WER labels + in-domain data; gains are single-digit-to-teens WERR; opaque about how much of the oracle ceiling is captured; tied to one ASR's acoustic features.
papers.code_available: No public code released (Amazon internal Alexa data).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Closest classical N-best selector, but it is SUPERVISED (trained BERT-conf + LTR) and never reports rho (fraction of oracle realized). Ours is training-free at inference over frozen-omni K-pools and its headline metric IS rho.
papers.kill_relevance: I1 (label-free selector): NO KILL — it is a trained/supervised selector, not label-free; needs WER-labeled training. I2 (audio-grounded training-free): NO KILL — uses acoustic features but supervised, not frozen-omni-native. I3 (abstaining/Goodhart): NO THREAT — no abstention/breakpoint. I4 (supply-stratified): NO THREAT — single fixed +LM supply, no supply stratification.

papers.title: Error Correction by Paying Attention to Both Acoustic and Confidence References for ASR (Shu, Hu, He, Shi, Wang, Dang)
papers.task: Non-autoregressive ASR error correction (rewrite) of N-best hypotheses; Mandarin ASR (CER).
papers.candidate_source_supply: Beam N-best from a fixed ASR (Conformer/Transformer on AISHELL-1); N-best candidates aligned via edit path. Single fixed supply.
papers.sees_audio: YES — uses the acoustic feature from the ASR encoder as a 'correct-pronunciation' reference, fused by cross-attention. Strongest audio-grounded paper in the family.
papers.gold_at_train: YES — reference transcripts to train the non-autoregressive corrector.
papers.training_required: YES — supervised corrector trained on AISHELL-1.
papers.scorer_inputs: Per-word confidence (Confidence Module measuring uncertainty of each N-best word to locate wrong positions) + acoustic encoder features + cross-attention over aligned N-best -> corrected tokens.
papers.selection_operator: Generative error correction (non-autoregressive rewrite), NOT pure N-best selection; the confidence module localizes wrong words and acoustic reference supplies replacements.
papers.comparators: ASR baseline (no correction); ablations removing acoustic reference and removing confidence reference.
papers.equal_budget: Not applicable / not equal-K selection; fixed N-best correction vs baseline.
papers.datasets_used: AISHELL-1 Mandarin (150/10/5 h train/dev/test).
papers.eval_protocol: CER on AISHELL-1 test; ablation shows both acoustic and confidence references contribute.
papers.headroom_evidence: Reduces error rate by 21% relative vs the ASR model on AISHELL-1; ablations confirm acoustic + confidence each help. No oracle-fraction reported.
papers.failure_modes: Trained per language/domain; generative rewrite can over-correct/hallucinate; Mandarin CER only; bound to the specific ASR's encoder (not a separate frozen verifier).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Closest instantiation of the I2 idea (audio grounding helps), but it is a TRAINED corrector reading its OWN ASR encoder; ours uses a SEPARATE frozen omni model as an independent verifier, training-free, and SELECTS rather than rewrites.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: NO KILL — generative corrector, not a label-free selector. I2 (audio-grounded): PARTIAL THREAT — demonstrates acoustic+confidence grounding yields +21% CER, i.e. the 'audio helps' idea is done, BUT supervised & tied to one ASR encoder, so it does NOT kill a TRAINING-FREE frozen-omni-native selector. I3: NO THREAT — word-level localization but no Goodhart/abstention. I4: NO THREAT — single supply, no stratification.

papers.title: Learning Word-Level Confidence for Subword End-to-End ASR (Li/Qiu, He, Zhang, ... Sainath, McGraw) — Confidence Estimation Module (CEM)
papers.task: Word/token-level confidence estimation for subword E2E ASR (calibration), not selection.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Decoder/beam output of an E2E ASR (optionally with LM shallow fusion); confidence computed over decoded tokens. Single system, no N-best selection.
papers.sees_audio: YES (indirectly) — CEM ingests internal encoder/attention/decoder features of the E2E ASR.
papers.gold_at_train: YES — word-piece correctness labels (derived via edit alignment to references) to train the CEM; paper notes non-unique WP tokenization makes labels noisy.
papers.training_required: YES — CEM is a lightweight trained add-on network.
papers.scorer_inputs: Encoder/attention/decoder features -> CEM -> per-token confidence; aggregated to word-level.
papers.selection_operator: Confidence calibration/thresholding; not an N-best selector (could feed one).
papers.comparators: Softmax/max-probability confidence baseline; other confidence estimators.
papers.equal_budget: N/A (confidence-quality task, not selection).
papers.datasets_used: LibriSpeech + Google in-house (Voice Search) sets.
papers.eval_protocol: Confidence-quality metrics (NCE, AUC-ROC / AUC-PR); shows CEM substantially beats softmax and mitigates overconfidence, with and without LM shallow fusion.
papers.headroom_evidence: Large NCE/AUC gains over softmax; addresses overconfidence. No WER/oracle-headroom-realization number (it does not select among hypotheses).
papers.failure_modes: Needs WP correctness labels (noisy from tokenization); confidence != selection; tied to internal features of one ASR; supervised.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Provides the confidence signal a selector would consume, but is (a) supervised and (b) calibration-only. Ours turns FROZEN-omni signals into an actual selector and reports oracle-headroom realization (rho).
papers.kill_relevance: I1: NO KILL — not a selector, and supervised. I2: PARTIAL relevance — audio-grounded confidence, but trained and internal-to-one-ASR, not frozen-omni-native; no kill. I3 (Goodhart/abstain): PARTIAL — directly tackles overconfidence (calibration), relevant to abstention, but single-task and supervised; no cross-task breakpoint; no kill. I4: NO THREAT — no supply stratification.

papers.title: Fast Entropy-Based Methods of Word-Level Confidence Estimation for End-to-End ASR (Laptev, Ginsburg, NVIDIA)
papers.task: Non-trainable (training-free) word-level confidence estimation for CTC and RNN-T E2E ASR.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Beam-lattice / per-frame posteriors of a single CTC or RNN-T ASR. Not N-best selection; supply is one ASR's frame posteriors.
papers.sees_audio: YES (indirectly) — entropy is computed from the acoustic model's per-frame posterior distribution.
papers.gold_at_train: NO — methods are non-trainable (closed-form entropy); optional threshold may use a dev set.
papers.training_required: NO — training-free entropy aggregation (one of very few training-free confidence methods; comparator anchor for our training-free framing).
papers.scorer_inputs: Per-frame entropy of posteriors, normalized and aggregated to per-unit/per-word confidence.
papers.selection_operator: Confidence thresholding for incorrect-word DETECTION; not an N-best selector.
papers.comparators: Maximum per-frame probability (softmax-max) confidence baseline.
papers.equal_budget: N/A (detection task).
papers.datasets_used: LibriSpeech test sets; Conformer-CTC and Conformer-RNN-T.
papers.eval_protocol: Incorrect-word detection quality (AUC/threshold-range analysis); reports separation of correct/incorrect distributions.
papers.headroom_evidence: Up to 2x (Conformer-CTC) and 4x (Conformer-RNN-T) better incorrect-word detection than max-probability, at similar compute, with a wider effective threshold range. No N-best selection / oracle realization.
papers.failure_modes: Requires access to a SPECIFIC ASR's frame posteriors/entropy (not available from a black-box frozen omni unless logprobs exposed); it detects, it does not select; not applied to K-pool selection.
papers.code_available: Yes — implemented in NVIDIA NeMo confidence estimation.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: The rare training-free confidence in this family, but it is (a) internal frame-entropy of ONE ASR and (b) word-error detection, not selection over external frozen-omni K-pools with a WER reward. We reuse the training-free spirit but as a SELECTOR with oracle-headroom accounting.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL THREAT — proves a training-free confidence signal exists, but never used to select over an N-best/K-pool nor to realize oracle headroom; no kill. I2 (audio-grounded training-free): PARTIAL THREAT — training-free AND audio-derived, the closest existing analog, BUT frame-level detection on one CTC/RNN-T, not a frozen-omni selector; no kill. I3: PARTIAL — better separation aids thresholding/abstention, but no Goodhart breakpoint; no kill. I4: NO THREAT — no supply stratification.

papers.title: NoRefER: a Referenceless Quality Metric for ASR via Semi-Supervised LM Fine-Tuning with Contrastive Learning (Yuksel et al., aiXplain)
papers.task: Referenceless (label-free at inference) quality scoring and intra-sample RANKING of ASR hypotheses — directly a label-free selector.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Text outputs from multiple ASR systems and/or multiple compression levels of one model (self-supervised ordering). Multi-system text supply; no audio.
papers.sees_audio: NO — text-only (fine-tuned MiniLMv2 / multilingual LM over hypothesis text).
papers.gold_at_train: Partial — self-supervised variant uses known quality ORDER between compression levels (no labels); semi-supervised variant adds a referenced (WER-labeled) dataset.
papers.training_required: YES — contrastive (Siamese, pairwise) fine-tuning of the LM.
papers.scorer_inputs: Hypothesis text only, encoded by the fine-tuned LM; pairwise comparison head.
papers.selection_operator: Pairwise ranking -> argmax = select best hypothesis among candidates WITHOUT references. This is the family's purest label-free selector.
papers.comparators: Reference-based WER (as correlation target); other referenceless metrics.
papers.equal_budget: Ranks whatever candidate set is given; not framed as equal-K oracle realization, but naturally operates over an N-best.
papers.datasets_used: Common Voice, multilingual (multiple languages).
papers.eval_protocol: Correlation with reference WER and with intra-sample rank; reported as 'high correlation' (abstract gives no exact Kendall/Pearson).
papers.headroom_evidence: Picks better hypothesis intra-sample without references; high correlation with WER. No explicit WERR/oracle-fraction number in the sources fetched.
papers.failure_modes: TEXT-ONLY -> blind to acoustics, cannot catch acoustically-plausible but wrong transcriptions (exactly the audio-grounded gap); requires contrastive training; may inherit LM/fluency bias (Goodhart risk toward fluent-but-wrong).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: The strongest existing label-free N-best selector = our I1, so it is the top I1 threat; BUT it is text-only and contrastively TRAINED. Our delta: audio-grounded via frozen omni, training-free at inference, and supply-stratified with rho accounting.
papers.kill_relevance: I1 (label-free selector): STRONGEST THREAT / ALREADY-DONE for the text-only case — a referenceless ranker that selects best-of-N without references already exists; our I1 must differentiate on audio grounding + training-free-at-inference + rho, or it is subsumed. I2 (audio-grounded): NO THREAT — sees no audio, so leaves the audio-grounded niche fully open. I3: NO THREAT — no abstention/breakpoint (and its fluency bias is itself a Goodhart vulnerability we can exploit). I4: NO THREAT — no supply stratification.

papers.title: HypR: A comprehensive study for ASR hypothesis revising with a reference corpus (Wang et al., NTUST)
papers.task: Benchmark corpus + study comparing N-best RERANKING vs error-CORRECTION methods for ASR hypothesis revising (English + Mandarin).
papers.candidate_source_supply: Beam N-best: 50 recognition hypotheses per utterance from ASR systems on each corpus; LM-decoded. Single fixed supply per corpus (no supply stratification).
papers.sees_audio: NO — the released HypR corpus is text N-best; the surveyed methods (LM rescoring, BERT, GPT-2, seq2seq correction) are text-based.
papers.gold_at_train: YES — references used both to build the corpus and to train the supervised rerankers/correctors.
papers.gold_at_test: NO (benchmark evaluation uses references only to score).
papers.training_required: YES for the reranking/correction methods studied (supervised).
papers.scorer_inputs: Hypothesis text (+ LM / BERT / GPT-2 scores); rerankers pick lowest-error, correctors rewrite.
papers.selection_operator: Both operators benchmarked: (a) reranking = argmax over rescored N-best; (b) error-correction = generative rewrite.
papers.comparators: LM rescoring, BERT, GPT-2, seq2seq correction, plus the ORACLE (lowest-WER in the 50-best) as the ceiling.
papers.equal_budget: Standardizes on 50-best across methods -> the closest thing to an equal-K comparison in the family, but not framed as rho realization.
papers.datasets_used: AISHELL-1 (Mandarin, CER), TED-LIUM 2 (English), LibriSpeech (English).
papers.eval_protocol: WER/CER of each method vs baseline and vs oracle across the 3 corpora at 50-best; notes LibriSpeech gap is largest (Transformer LM more robust).
papers.headroom_evidence: Provides the oracle upper bound at N=50 across three corpora and shows a LARGE residual gap between practical rerankers/correctors and the oracle. Confirms LM decoding helps but does not close the oracle gap.
papers.failure_modes: Benchmarks SUPERVISED text methods only; no audio grounding; single supply level; residual oracle gap unexplained/unrealized; Mandarin+English but clean-ish.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: The family's headroom/oracle benchmark = our I4/I1 measurement frame, but at ONE supply level, text-only, supervised methods. Our delta: stratify oracle headroom H(c) by capability-supply, audio-grounded, training-free.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL THREAT — standardizes N-best reranking-vs-oracle, so any I1 selector must beat its benchmarked rerankers; but its methods are supervised & text-only, and it shows the oracle gap is UNCLOSED (headroom NOT eaten). I2: NO THREAT — no audio grounding. I3: NO THREAT — no Goodhart/abstention. I4 (supply-stratified): CLOSEST but NO KILL — it fixes one supply and never stratifies by capability-supply, so the supply-conditional H(c) question is untouched.

papers.title: ProGRes: Prompted Generative Rescoring on ASR n-Best (Tur et al.)
papers.task: Training-free (zero-shot, prompt-based) LLM rescoring that also EXPANDS the N-best with LLM-generated new hypotheses, then selects.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Beam N-best EXPANDED by LLM-generated new hypotheses (supply-AUGMENTING). Combines recognizer confidence + LLM sequence score + prompt-generated candidates. Supply is deliberately grown, not held fixed.
papers.sees_audio: NO — LLMs (Llama-3, GPT-3.5/4 Turbo) see text n-best + scalar confidence only; no audio.
papers.gold_at_train: NO — zero-shot prompting, no task-specific training.
papers.training_required: NO — training-free / zero-shot (uses off-the-shelf instruction-tuned LLMs).
papers.scorer_inputs: Recognizer confidence scores + LLM sequence log-prob + LLM-generated hypotheses; combined score.
papers.selection_operator: Argmax over combined (confidence + LLM-score) over the EXPANDED candidate set; a training-free selector but over an enlarged pool.
papers.comparators: First-pass baseline; LLM-sequence-scoring-only; confidence-only; different generator LLMs (Llama-3-Instruct vs GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 Turbo).
papers.equal_budget: NOT equal-K vs a frozen pool — it ADDS hypotheses, so gains partly come from expanded supply, not pure selection. Explicitly supply-augmenting.
papers.datasets_used: Multiple speech recognizers / standard ASR sets (English).
papers.eval_protocol: Relative WER improvement across recognizers; compares generator LLMs.
papers.headroom_evidence: Achieves 5%-25% relative WER improvement, but explicitly states 'a significant gap compared to the oracle remains' -> headroom NOT eaten even after LLM expansion.
papers.failure_modes: LLM latency/cost; changes supply (not pure selection over a frozen pool); text-only so blind to acoustics; large residual oracle gap; can favor fluent-but-wrong (Goodhart).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Closest training-free LLM selector, but it EXPANDS the pool (violates equal-K) and is text-only. Our delta: hold K fixed over a frozen-omni pool, audio-grounded verification, and report rho — so we can attribute gains to SELECTION not supply growth.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL THREAT — training-free LLM selection over n-best exists (5-25% WERR), so pure-text training-free selection is partly done; but it augments supply (not equal-K) and leaves a large oracle gap. I2: NO THREAT — text-only, no audio. I3: NO THREAT — no explicit Goodhart/abstention. I4 (supply-stratified): DIRECT RELEVANCE / PARTIAL THREAT — by generating new hypotheses it literally changes capability-supply and realizes more headroom, evidencing supply-conditionality, BUT it never systematically stratifies/measures H(c); it motivates rather than kills I4.

papers.title: Identifying and Calibrating Overconfidence in Noisy Speech Recognition
papers.task: Detect and calibrate ASR OVERCONFIDENCE under additive noise (SNR sweep) via a post-hoc classifier + selective temperature scaling.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Single Whisper-medium-en decode under synthetic temporally-modulated noise across 29 SNR levels (+10 to -18 dB). Not N-best selection; supply is one decode under a NOISE-conditioned axis.
papers.sees_audio: YES — confidence/logits come from Whisper's acoustic-conditioned decoder; the whole study is about acoustic-noise degradation.
papers.gold_at_train: YES — token correctness labels to train the overconfidence classifier and fit temperature.
papers.training_required: YES — lightweight 3.4M-param add-on (binary overconfidence classifier + token-level temperature), post-hoc, does not modify Whisper.
papers.scorer_inputs: Whisper token logits/features -> overconfidence classifier -> selective token-level temperature scaling.
papers.selection_operator: Calibration + selective temperature (abstention-oriented reliability), NOT N-best selection.
papers.comparators: Uncalibrated softmax; global (single) temperature scaling.
papers.equal_budget: N/A (calibration task).
papers.datasets_used: Train: LibriTTS clean-100 + synthetic noise (29 SNRs). Eval: R-SPIN corpus (400 phonetically balanced sentences).
papers.eval_protocol: ECE, NCE, NLL, EER across SNRs; focuses on overconfidence (not just ECE).
papers.headroom_evidence: At low SNR, 10-20% of tokens wrongly predicted with conf>0.7; 22.4% overconfident at -18 dB pre-calibration. Method: 58% relative ECE reduction (0.086->0.036), NCE 0.064->0.192, overconfident mass 11.1%->6.6% (in -18..-5 dB).
papers.failure_modes: Trained calibrator needs correctness labels; single-task ASR only (not cross-task); calibration, not selection; specific to Whisper features.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Closest to I3 (the noise/over-optimization edge = Goodhart regime, and it operates in exactly our snr5 noise band), but it CALIBRATES a single ASR's confidence rather than ABSTAINING/selecting across a cross-task frozen-omni pool, and it is supervised. Our delta: cross-task abstaining SELECTOR with explicit Goodhart-breakpoint detection, training-free.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: NO THREAT — not a selector. I2: PARTIAL — audio-grounded confidence under noise, but trained and single-ASR; no kill. I3 (abstaining/Goodhart): STRONGEST THREAT among confidence work — directly detects overconfidence at the noise edge and quantifies it (22.4% overconfident @ -18 dB; 58% ECE cut), i.e. 'confidence breaks under noise' is established; BUT it is single-task ASR calibration, supervised, NOT a cross-task abstaining selector with breakpoint detection -> does not kill I3, it validates I3's premise. I4: PARTIAL — SNR is a degradation axis (a form of condition stratification) but it stratifies by NOISE, not by capability-supply; no kill.

families.saturation_note: Family status: MATURE on supervised text/confidence rescoring, but the specific combination our four identity candidates target is UNCLAIMED. (1) Confidence estimation is well-developed: calibration and NCE/AUC quality are solved offline (Li/Qiu CEM 2021; Laptev entropy 2023 is the rare TRAINING-FREE one; overconfidence-in-noise 2025 quantifies the noise breakpoint we care about). (2) Learning-to-rank / discriminative rescoring realizes only a MODEST fraction of N-best oracle headroom (single-digit-to-~14% WERR; Wu 2022) and ALWAYS needs supervised WER-labeled training. (3) The oracle gap is EXPLICITLY NOT closed: HypR (Interspeech 2024, 50-best, AISHELL-1/TED-LIUM 2/LibriSpeech) shows a large residual gap to oracle; ProGRes (SLT 2024) states 'a significant gap compared to the oracle remains' even after LLM supply expansion. (4) A pure LABEL-FREE selector exists (NoRefER, Interspeech 2023) but is TEXT-ONLY and contrastively trained. Net: no paper in this family simultaneously (a) selects fully TRAINING-FREE at inference over a FROZEN omni model's K-pool, (b) grounds selection in FROZEN-OMNI-NATIVE audio signals (Shu/CEM use one ASR's own internal features; NoRefER/LLM rescoring ignore audio), (c) performs cross-task ABSTAINING selection with explicit Goodhart-breakpoint detection (overconfidence-noise is single-task calibration), or (d) STRATIFIES headroom by capability-supply H(c). The headroom is demonstrably NOT eaten; the differentiators are open.
gaps: SUPPLY-CONDITIONALITY untouched: every paper uses ONE fixed candidate supply (beam n-best, or n-best re-scored by an LM). None stratify oracle headroom H(c) by capability-supply (bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval). ProGRes only expands supply ad hoc via LLM generation; HypR fixes 50-best. Directly leaves I4 open.

TRAINING-FREE-AT-INFERENCE SELECTION over a frozen omni K-pool is absent: the selectors here are SUPERVISED (BERT-conf+LTR Wu; corrector Shu; CEM Li/Qiu; contrastive NoRefER; overconfidence classifier 2025). The only training-free members are Laptev's entropy confidence (DETECTION on one ASR's frame posteriors, not selection) and ProGRes (prompting, but text-only + supply-augmenting). No one selects training-free over a frozen omni's K-pool with a verifiable WER reward.

AUDIO-GROUNDED SELECTION via a SEPARATE frozen omni verifier is missing: audio grounding only appears as a SINGLE ASR's own internal encoder features (Shu, CEM, Laptev, overconfidence-2025). Using an independent frozen omni model's native signals as a decorrelated verifier over another model's K-pool is not covered. NoRefER/HypR/ProGRes are text-only. Leaves I2 open.

EQUAL-BUDGET / rho ACCOUNTING absent: papers report WERR vs a baseline, NOT the fraction of oracle headroom realized (rho) under fixed K. Oracle is used only as a passive ceiling (HypR) or noted as an unclosed gap (ProGRes). No equal-K controlled selector-vs-oracle-realization protocol like our C-ASR-V2.

CROSS-TASK ABSTAINING / GOODHART-BREAKPOINT DETECTION absent: overconfidence-in-noise (2025) establishes that confidence breaks under noise (our snr5 regime) but only as SINGLE-TASK calibration; no cross-task abstaining SELECTOR with explicit Goodhart-breakpoint detection. Leaves I3 open.

REWARD-GUIDED / inference-time-optimization framing absent: all are discriminative or generative rescoring; none frame selection as reward-guided inference-time optimization over a frozen model (our thesis).

MANDARIN/NOISE K-POOL SELECTION under-studied: Chinese ASR appears only clean (AISHELL-1 in Shu, HypR); noise appears only in single-decode calibration (overconfidence-2025). Selection over noisy Mandarin K-pools (aishell-1/thchs-30 + snr) is uncovered.

FLUENCY BIAS as a Goodhart failure of text-only selectors (NoRefER, LLM rescoring) is acknowledged implicitly (LM-robustness effect in HypR) but never diagnosed as a breakpoint — an opening for our audio-grounded, abstaining design.

families.family: Best-of-N scaling, reward overoptimization, and test-time compute (with emphasis on speech/audio applications)

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
papers.task: Characterize how optimizing a PROXY reward model (via best-of-n vs RL) degrades the GOLD reward (Goodhart) as a function of optimization distance; fit scaling laws in KL, RM size, RM data size, policy size.
papers.candidate_source_supply: bare-model sampling — BoN draws N samples from a fixed policy and argmaxes the proxy RM; RL optimizes the same policy with KL penalty. Text-only synthetic InstructGPT-style setup.
papers.sees_audio: no (text-only; a large 'gold' RM labels a synthetic preference task; no audio anywhere).
papers.gold_at_train: yes for the RM pipeline — a fixed gold RM generates labels used to TRAIN the proxy RM at multiple sizes. The BoN/RL selection itself trains nothing.
papers.gold_at_test: yes as EVALUATOR only — gold RM score is the y-axis ground truth; the optimizer never sees gold, only the proxy. (This is the clean information-boundary that our selectors must also respect.)
papers.training_required: proxy RM must be trained; BoN selection given a proxy RM is training-free. RL requires policy optimization.
papers.scorer_inputs: proxy reward model scalar over text (no reference, no audio).
papers.selection_operator: best-of-n = argmax proxy reward over N samples; RL = KL-regularized policy gradient.
papers.comparators: BoN vs RL as the two optimization operators; swept over RM param count, RM dataset size, policy param count, and KL-penalty coefficient.
papers.equal_budget: compared on a shared budget axis d = sqrt(KL) (nats); for BoN KL ≈ log N − (N−1)/N. This is the canonical 'equal-KL' budgeting the whole field inherited.
papers.datasets_used: single synthetic gold-RM labeling task on InstructGPT prompts; text-only. No standard NLP/speech benchmark.
papers.eval_protocol: gold reward plotted vs d=sqrt(KL); fit closed forms; measure onset of overoptimization (gold peaks then falls).
papers.headroom_evidence: Reported functional forms: BoN gold R_bon(d)=d(alpha_bon − beta_bon·d); RL gold R_RL(d)=d(alpha_RL − beta_RL·log d). Gold rises then DECLINES past a KL point (overoptimization). Key numeric qualitative result: as a function of KL, RL is SLOWER than BoN at both optimization and overoptimization — so KL is not a fair cross-method budget. Coefficients scale smoothly (log-linear) with RM parameter count; smaller RMs and smaller RM datasets overoptimize sooner.
papers.failure_modes: Goodhart: past a KL threshold, proxy up but gold down; smaller/weaker proxy RMs break earlier; KL is an unreliable common currency across BoN vs RL.
papers.code_available: No official code released by authors (OpenAI); the phenomenon has been reproduced by follow-ups (RM ensembles, WARM).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: This is the THEORY anchor for the shape of the headroom/overoptimization curve, but with a LEARNED scalar proxy RM on text. Ours uses a VERIFIABLE reward (WER/exact-match) — no proxy-gold divergence by construction — and measures oracle-headroom REALIZATION RATE (rho) on SPEECH/omni pools, not proxy-vs-gold gap. Their d=sqrt(KL) budget axis is directly reusable for our equal-K sweeps.
papers.kill_relevance: I1 (label-free N-best selector): no-threat on speech; supplies the BoN budgeting formalism we build on. I2 (audio-grounded selector): no-threat (no audio). I3 (constrained/abstaining + Goodhart-breakpoint): PARTIAL — it is the origin of the Goodhart-breakpoint we want to DETECT; but only for learned-proxy RMs, not verifiable rewards, so our I3 with a verifiable scorer is a different (and arguably safer) regime. I4 (supply×selector): no-threat — single supply, no capability-stratification.

papers.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
papers.venue_year: arXiv Aug 2024 (2408.03314); widely cited as ICLR-2025-era
papers.task: Compute-optimal test-time scaling: allocate inference compute between (a) searching against a process-reward verifier and (b) adaptively revising the model's own proposal, conditioned on prompt difficulty.
papers.candidate_source_supply: bare-model sampling + PRM-guided search (beam / lookahead tree) + sequential self-revision. Base LM = PaLM-2 / Gemma-class on MATH.
papers.sees_audio: no (text math reasoning).
papers.gold_at_train: yes — a process reward model (PRM) and a revision model are FINETUNED using gold-answer rollouts.
papers.gold_at_test: no gold at test for selection; the PRM (learned) plus majority voting stands in for gold.
papers.training_required: yes — PRM + revision model are trained (this is the key non-training-free cost).
papers.scorer_inputs: text; PRM scores intermediate reasoning steps (no reference, no audio).
papers.selection_operator: best-of-N weighted, beam search, and lookahead search against the PRM; plus adaptive proposal revision (self-refine chain).
papers.comparators: compute-optimal allocation vs a naive best-of-N baseline; and a FLOPs-matched comparison vs a 14x larger pretrained model.
papers.equal_budget: YES — this is the paper's core contribution: FLOPs/compute-matched evaluation is the whole methodology.
papers.datasets_used: MATH benchmark; difficulty binned into 5 quantiles.
papers.eval_protocol: accuracy vs test-time compute budget, STRATIFIED BY QUESTION DIFFICULTY (easy→hard).
papers.headroom_evidence: Compute-optimal strategy is >4x more efficient than the best-of-N baseline at matched compute. On easy/medium problems (where the small base has non-trivial success), test-time compute at matched FLOPs BEATS a 14x larger model. On the hardest problems, pretraining/bigger-model still wins — efficacy is difficulty-conditional (revision helps easy, search helps hard).
papers.failure_modes: On hardest problems test-time compute does NOT substitute for a larger base; verifier search saturates; the optimal method flips with difficulty, so a fixed policy is suboptimal.
papers.code_available: No official author code (Google DeepMind); open reproductions exist.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Establishes DIFFICULTY-conditional efficacy of test-time compute with a TRAINED PRM on text math. Our I4 conditions on a different axis — CAPABILITY SUPPLY (bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval), not item difficulty — and is training-free on frozen speech/omni pools with verifiable reward. Their equal-FLOPs discipline is the standard we must meet for equal-K claims.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: no-threat on speech; motivates verifier-guided selection generally. I2: no-threat (no audio). I3: PARTIAL — 'which method when' anticipates a constrained/adaptive selector, but no explicit abstention or Goodhart-breakpoint. I4: PARTIAL/PROXIMAL — it is the strongest prior on CONDITIONAL headroom, but conditions on difficulty (per-item), not on capability supply (per-configuration); our supply-stratified H(c) is the unclaimed axis, so it sharpens rather than kills I4.

papers.title: Inference-Time Reward Hacking in Large Language Models
papers.task: Characterize and mitigate reward hacking that arises purely at INFERENCE time when overoptimizing a misspecified proxy reward via best-of-n and its soft/Poisson variants; find the optimal hedging parameter.
papers.candidate_source_supply: bare-model sampling — N samples from a fixed LLM scored by a fixed proxy reward. Text (math, reasoning, human-preference).
papers.sees_audio: no.
papers.gold_at_train: no policy/RM training; the proxy reward is a pre-existing trained RM.
papers.gold_at_test: gold/true reward used only to EVALUATE the reward-distortion curves; the selector sees only the proxy.
papers.training_required: no — fully inference-time; HedgeTune only tunes one scalar hedging parameter.
papers.scorer_inputs: proxy reward model over text (no reference, no audio).
papers.selection_operator: Best-of-n (BoN), Soft-Best-of-n (SBoN, reward-tilted sampling), and Best-of-Poisson (BoP, a near-exact approximation of the optimal reward-KL policy); HedgeTune picks the optimal inference-time parameter.
papers.comparators: BoN vs SBoN vs BoP; naive vs HedgeTune-hedged, on the reward-vs-distortion (KL) frontier.
papers.equal_budget: analyzed on the reward-KL / distortion tradeoff — budget = KL / effective N; hedging chosen at the optimal point.
papers.datasets_used: math, reasoning, and human-preference setups (text; e.g. AlpacaFarm-style preference).
papers.eval_protocol: true reward vs proxy reward as N / tilt increases; reward-distortion frontier; locate the hacking onset.
papers.headroom_evidence: Central result: true reward first RISES then DECLINES as inference optimization increases — proven to be an INEVITABLE property of a broad class of inference-time mechanisms including BoN and BoP. Hedging (SBoN/BoP with the HedgeTune-optimal parameter) mitigates the decline and yields a strictly better reward-distortion tradeoff; BoP gives a near-exact optimal reward-KL policy.
papers.failure_modes: Naive large-N BoN overoptimizes the proxy and gold falls; the peak-then-fall is unavoidable without hedging; requires a well-specified proxy for the tuned optimum to be meaningful.
papers.code_available: Not confirmed in fetch — check OpenReview hSX7Dd8dxy for a code link (HedgeTune presented as an algorithm).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: This is the formal backbone of I3's 'Goodhart-breakpoint detection': it PROVES the peak-then-decline is inevitable for BoN-class selectors and gives a tuning rule (HedgeTune) — essentially an abstain/hedge trigger. But it is TEXT + LEARNED PROXY reward. Our I3 wants the same breakpoint on SPEECH with a VERIFIABLE reward, where the classic proxy-hacking peak may not appear the same way — so our contribution shifts from 'proxy hacking' to 'cross-task/constraint abstention', a genuinely different failure surface.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: no-threat on speech; frames the risk of pure-N scaling. I2: no-threat (no audio). I3 (abstaining + Goodhart-breakpoint): STRONGEST THREAT in this set — HedgeTune already formalizes the optimal inference-time hedge/stop, so the DETECTION-and-hedge idea is not novel per se; our differentiator must be verifiable-reward speech + explicit abstention + supply-conditioning, not 'we noticed the peak'. I4: no-threat — single supply, no capability stratification.

papers.title: Scaling Auditory Cognition via Test-Time Compute in Audio Language Models
papers.task: Apply five training-free test-time-compute (TTC) strategies to FROZEN audio LLMs on auditory-cognition tasks (audio-event recognition, noisy speech comprehension, overlapping-speech digit recall).
papers.candidate_source_supply: bare-model sampling — temperature sweep 0-2.0 (0.2 steps) — plus beam search (2-7 beams). Frozen audio LLMs; no retrieval, no +LM.
papers.sees_audio: YES — models receive the audio waveform directly with pre/post-question prompts; no transcription-to-text intermediary. This is the key property matching our frozen-omni pools.
papers.gold_at_train: none (no training).
papers.gold_at_test: no reference/gold at selection; an external GPT-4o judge scores candidates for the two verifier variants (not gold, an LLM judge).
papers.training_required: no — all five methods are inference-only over off-the-shelf models.
papers.scorer_inputs: majority-vote = answer text; BS-W = decoder log-likelihood; LLM-verifier variants = GPT-4o scoring the responses (large external omni judge).
papers.selection_operator: (1) chain-of-thought, (2) temperature majority vote, (3) beam-search weighted log-likelihood (BS-W), (4) GPT-4o-verifier top-1, (5) GPT-4o-verifier weighted sum.
papers.comparators: five TTC methods vs no-TTC baseline across five audio LLMs (Qwen2-Audio, Audio-Flamingo 2, Gemini-2.0-Flash, Gemini-1.5-Pro, GPT-4o); human baseline.
papers.equal_budget: NO — temperature sweep vs beam-count vs verifier calls are not K-matched; N differs by method (a gap vs our equal-K discipline).
papers.datasets_used: self-collected auditory-cognition database, 10 participants, 3 tasks, with background noise and overlapping speech. Non-standard, small.
papers.eval_protocol: accuracy per task, before/after TTC, difficulty-stratified (Task1 easy → Task3 hard).
papers.headroom_evidence: Qwen2-Audio 36.7% → 50.0% overall with BS-W (+36% rel), Task-3 up to 41.7% (+66.8%). Audio-Flamingo 2 40.0% → 66.7% on Task-2 with GPT-4o-verifier-top-1 (+150% rel), Task-3 58.3% (+133%). Gains concentrate on the HARDER tasks (difficulty-conditional). Humans beat all models except GPT-4o on overlapped speech.
papers.failure_modes: tiny bespoke dataset (10 participants), narrow synthetic tasks; not equal-budget; verifier variants depend on a large external GPT-4o judge (not a frozen-core-native signal); no oracle-headroom / realization-rate framing; results not on standard benchmarks.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: This is the CLOSEST published prior art to I1/I2: training-free test-time SELECTION over frozen audio LLM pools that SEE AUDIO, including an (external) verifier. But it lives on a non-standard 10-person DB, uses a large external GPT-4o judge rather than the frozen core's own native signal, has no equal-K, no verifiable reward, and no oracle-headroom-realization (rho) metric. Ours: standard speech benchmarks, verifiable WER/EM reward, equal-K, paired-bootstrap CIs, supply-stratified H(c), and rho as the primary metric.
papers.kill_relevance: I1 (label-free N-best selector over frozen audio pools): PARTIAL THREAT — they literally do majority/verifier selection on frozen audio LLMs (+36% to +150% rel), so the CONCEPT is demonstrated; but on a bespoke 10-person DB with no headroom-realization framing, so it does NOT eat our headroom on standard sets. I2 (audio-grounded selector via frozen omni-native signal): PARTIAL — their GPT-4o verifier is an omni judge, but it is a large EXTERNAL model, not the frozen core's own native likelihood/embedding; leaves the 'frozen-core-native audio-grounded signal' open. I3: no-threat (no abstention/constraint). I4: no-threat on supply, though they do difficulty-condition.

papers.title: Re-evaluating Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding for Automatic Speech Recognition (and Speech Translation)
papers.task: Apply Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) selection over sampled hypotheses to modern ASR and ST (Whisper family), re-testing the belief that MBR helps only text-to-text.
papers.candidate_source_supply: bare-model sampling — epsilon sampling (eps=0.01, temp=1.0) from Whisper, N up to 64. Single supply.
papers.sees_audio: NO for the SELECTION step — MBR reranks using pairwise text utility among the N hypotheses; audio is used only to generate the samples, not to score them.
papers.gold_at_train: none.
papers.gold_at_test: no reference — MBR is a reference-free internal-consensus selector.
papers.training_required: no — 'does not require any additional training'.
papers.scorer_inputs: text only — pairwise BLEU utility between candidate hypotheses (consensus).
papers.selection_operator: MBR: argmax over candidates of expected utility (mean pairwise BLEU) against the sampled set.
papers.comparators: MBR vs beam search vs oracle (lowest-WER among the 64 samples).
papers.equal_budget: N=64 main; gains already appear at N=4-8 (relevant to our N<=8 regime).
papers.datasets_used: ASR: LibriSpeech, VoxPopuli, AMI-IHM, Japanese ReazonSpeech; ST: CoVoST2 ja->en, FLEURS en->ja.
papers.eval_protocol: WER (En) / CER (Ja) for ASR; BLEU/ROUGE-L/BLEURT/MetricX for ST; multiple SNR levels.
papers.headroom_evidence: LibriSpeech (Whisper-large-v3): beam 0.042 WER -> MBR 0.033 -> ORACLE(N=64) 0.013 — MBR realizes ~0.009 of the 0.029 oracle headroom (~31%). VoxPopuli (SNR0) 0.117 -> 0.098. Japanese ReazonSpeech (SNR0) 0.305 -> 0.291 CER (oracle 0.149 — huge unrealized gap). ST: CoVoST2 ja->en 18.6 -> 22.5 BLEU (+3.9); FLEURS en->ja 8.2 -> 11.7 BLEU (+3.5).
papers.failure_modes: AMI-IHM DEGRADES (0.380 -> 0.568 WER) on <6-word utterances where BLEU utility is unreliable — a real Goodhart-adjacent failure. Realizes only ~1/3 of oracle headroom on clean LibriSpeech; even less under heavy noise (0.291 vs 0.149 oracle).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: MBR is EXACTLY one of our already-implemented comparators (pairwise MBR). This paper is essentially our comparator applied to Whisper ASR/ST on the very tasks we hold (LibriSpeech, CoVoST2, FLEURS). It confirms a LARGE residual oracle headroom (~2/3 unrealized on clean, more under noise) that a text-only consensus selector cannot reach — precisely the gap an audio-grounded (I2) or supply-stratified (I4) selector targets.
papers.kill_relevance: I1 (label-free N-best selector on speech pools): PARTIAL — it demonstrates the exact I1 mechanism (MBR) on speech, so 'MBR on speech N-best' is NOT novel; BUT it realizes only ~31% of oracle headroom (LibriSpeech), so it CONFIRMS rather than EATS the headroom — it is a baseline we already have, not a kill. I2 (audio-grounded): no-threat — text-only consensus ignores the audio, leaving the audio-grounded gain fully open. I3: no-threat, though the AMI <6-word degradation is exactly the breakpoint I3 would abstain on. I4: no-threat — single bare-sampling supply.

papers.title: HyPoradise: An Open Baseline for Generative Speech Recognition with Large Language Models
papers.task: Generative error correction (H2T): an LLM REWRITES the true transcription from an ASR N-best list (generation, not selection) — can emit tokens absent from the N-best.
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam-lattice — top-5 hypotheses from beam-size-60 decoding (i.e. +implicit LM from the ASR). Single supply.
papers.sees_audio: NO — the LLM sees only the text N-best hypotheses, never the audio.
papers.gold_at_train: YES — trained on 334K (N-best, gold-transcript) pairs; this is a supervised mapping.
papers.training_required: YES — fine-tune T5-large (H2T-ft) or LoRA-adapt LLaMA-13B (H2T-LoRA); zero-shot was weak. This VIOLATES the training-free constraint.
papers.scorer_inputs: text N-best (no audio, no reference at test).
papers.selection_operator: NOT selection — a generative H2T rewrite; it can produce corrections outside the N-best set (why it can beat the selection oracle).
papers.comparators: baseline top-1, LM-rerank, N-best oracle o_nb, compositional oracle o_cp.
papers.equal_budget: n/a — generation, not K-selection.
papers.datasets_used: WSJ, CHiME-4, Tedlium-3, LibriSpeech test-clean/test-other, CommonVoice-accent, ATIS (11 sub-corpora).
papers.eval_protocol: WER% per corpus vs o_nb and o_cp.
papers.headroom_evidence: H2T-LoRA SURPASSES the N-best selection oracle o_nb on several sets: WSJ 3.8 vs o_nb 4.1 (baseline 4.5); CHiME-4 6.6 vs o_nb 9.1 (baseline 11.1); CommonVoice-accent 11.0 vs o_nb 11.4 (baseline 14.8); ATIS 2.7 vs o_nb 5.2 (baseline 8.3). It does NOT beat o_nb on LibriSpeech test-clean (1.7 vs o_nb 1.0) or test-other (3.8 vs o_nb 2.7). Compositional oracle o_cp (e.g. CHiME-4 2.8, WSJ 1.2) remains below.
papers.failure_modes: requires training + domain-matched gold pairs; text-only (ignores audio); on clean LibriSpeech it stays ABOVE the selection oracle; generation can hallucinate on low-N/OOD.
papers.code_available: YES — dataset + baseline code open-sourced (Hypotheses-Paradise repo).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: HyPoradise reframes the ceiling: a TRAINED generative rewriter can beat the N-best SELECTION oracle o_nb (because it rewrites, not selects). This is the sharpest threat to I1's 'oracle headroom is the ceiling' framing — IF training is allowed. Under our TRAINING-FREE constraint, a pure selector is still bounded by o_nb, so HyPoradise does not kill training-free selection; it defines the trained upper competitor / a baseline we should run to size the training-free deficit.
papers.kill_relevance: I1 (label-free N-best SELECTOR): FRAMING THREAT — proves the selection oracle o_nb is NOT the true ceiling when training is permitted (CHiME-4 6.6 < o_nb 9.1), which undercuts 'headroom = o_nb' unless we hold the training-free constraint explicit; it does not eat the training-FREE selector's value. I2 (audio-grounded): no-threat (text-only). I3: no-threat. I4: no-threat (single beam supply).

papers.title: Read What You Hear: Reference-Free Hypotheses Evaluation with Acoustic Discrepancy (READ)
papers.task: Reference-free, TRAINING-FREE evaluation/selection AND refinement of ASR hypotheses by measuring fine-grained ACOUSTIC DISCREPANCY between the speech signal and each text hypothesis.
papers.candidate_source_supply: ASR N-best / hypotheses; READ scores them; also drives refinement. Supply as reported = model hypotheses (bare/beam).
papers.sees_audio: YES — uses a PRETRAINED autoregressive TTS model to compute the conditional likelihood of the SPEECH tokens given a text hypothesis; the resulting NLL sequence is the acoustic-discrepancy map. This is the frozen-generative-speech-model-as-scorer mechanism.
papers.gold_at_train: none — the TTS scorer is pretrained and FROZEN.
papers.gold_at_test: no reference — grounds only in the input speech signal.
papers.training_required: NO — explicitly 'without additional training'.
papers.scorer_inputs: AUDIO (speech tokens) + candidate text -> per-token NLL from a frozen TTS model (audio-grounded, reference-free).
papers.selection_operator: rank/select the hypothesis with lowest acoustic discrepancy (NLL); plus hypothesis REFINEMENT guided by the NLL-spike locations (error localization).
papers.comparators: baselines incl. LM rescoring / confidence methods; correlation with true error positions; WER vs baseline.
papers.equal_budget: not detailed in fetch (N size not stated).
papers.datasets_used: LibriSpeech (clean + noisy conditions).
papers.eval_protocol: WER; token-level correlation of NLL spikes with recognition errors; noise robustness.
papers.headroom_evidence: Up to 20% RELATIVE error-rate reduction from applying READ (selection + refinement), with the largest gains under NOISY conditions; NLL spikes localize to misrecognized segments.
papers.failure_modes: depends on the frozen TTS model's quality/domain and NLL calibration; exact absolute WER and oracle-gap numbers sparse in fetch; single-supply, ASR-only.
papers.code_available: Not verified in fetch (X-LANCE typically releases).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: READ is the DIRECT prior art for I2: an AUDIO-GROUNDED, TRAINING-FREE selector that uses a FROZEN generative speech model's likelihood as the reward signal on the speech itself — almost exactly I2's mechanism, and its strongest gains are under NOISE, which is precisely our librispeech-snr5 regime. Deltas: READ uses a TTS acoustic-continuation likelihood (not an omni-native embedding/verifier), is ASR-only, single-supply, has no Goodhart/abstain (I3), no supply-stratification (I4), and no oracle-headroom-REALIZATION-RATE (rho) framing.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: no-threat directly (it is strictly stronger than label-free — it is audio-grounded). I2 (audio-grounded training-free selector via frozen speech signal): STRONGEST THREAT in the whole family — near-identical mechanism, training-free, 20% rel WERR incl. noise on LibriSpeech; our I2 differentiation MUST be crisp (omni-native embedding/verifier not TTS-likelihood; verifiable-reward error-decorrelation; supply-stratification) or I2 is largely pre-empted. I3: no-threat (no abstention). I4: no-threat (single supply).

papers.title: Best-of-N TTS Evaluation is Confounded by ASR Family Alignment
papers.venue_year: ICML 2026 Workshop on ML for Audio (arXiv Jul 2026, 2607.08256)
papers.task: Best-of-N selection of zero-shot TTS outputs via an ASR verifier (pick lowest-WER synthesis); expose that a verifier's apparent quality — and its oracle-headroom recovery — is CONFOUNDED by ASR-family alignment with the evaluator; propose cross-family rank ensembles.
papers.candidate_source_supply: bare TTS sampling — N candidates synthesized by a frozen zero-shot TTS (F5-TTS). Single-supply.
papers.sees_audio: YES — the verifier is a frozen ASR model that TRANSCRIBES the synthesized AUDIO to compute WER against the intended text (audio-grounded verifier).
papers.gold_at_train: none.
papers.gold_at_test: the intended text (the TTS prompt) IS the reference for computing synthesis WER — so the scorer has a task-defined target (a legitimate self-supervision for TTS, distinct from ASR where the transcript would be leakage).
papers.training_required: no.
papers.scorer_inputs: synthesized AUDIO -> frozen-ASR transcript -> WER vs intended text; verifier is a frozen ASR (Whisper / wav2vec2 / HuBERT).
papers.selection_operator: best-of-N = lowest verifier WER; plus two proposed CROSS-FAMILY ensembles: rank-averaging and conjunctive max-rank.
papers.comparators: single-family verifier vs cross-family ensemble vs oracle headroom; three independent evaluators (Whisper, wav2vec2, HuBERT).
papers.equal_budget: N=10 fixed.
papers.datasets_used: LibriSpeech-PC test-clean; F5-TTS; secondary metrics SIM-o and UTMOS.
papers.eval_protocol: mean WER across 3 independent ASR evaluators; fraction of oracle headroom recovered; SIM-o/UTMOS non-degradation check.
papers.headroom_evidence: SAME-family verifier-evaluator pairs recover 2-3x MORE oracle headroom than cross-family pairs, despite near-identical representations (linear CKA 0.978) — i.e. the recovered 'headroom' is partly an identity/lineage artifact, not true quality. Cross-family ensembles reach 1.61% mean WER (-12% rel); best single verifier 1.72% (-16.5% rel); no SIM-o/UTMOS degradation.
papers.failure_modes: verifier-evaluator FAMILY ALIGNMENT inflates apparent headroom recovery by 2-3x (Goodhart-adjacent: choosing a same-lineage verifier games a same-lineage evaluator); a single audio verifier's gains can be a measurement artifact.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: The KEY CAUTIONARY paper for our omni-as-reward / I2: an audio-grounded verifier's measured oracle-headroom recovery is CONFOUNDED (2-3x inflation) when verifier and evaluator share lineage. This is a direct, empirical instance of the failure our omni-verifier error-DECORRELATION constraint (delta_corr) is meant to bound — and it flags an acute risk in our setup, where Qwen3-Omni-30B both GENERATES the pool and could SCORE it (maximal same-family alignment). Delta: they study TTS generation, we study ASR/understanding selection; the confound generalizes.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: no-threat (TTS synthesis, not N-best text selection). I2 (audio-grounded frozen-omni verifier): THREAT + VALIDATION — it shows the audio-verifier BoN DOES recover oracle headroom (1.61% WER, -12% rel) BUT that the recovered amount is 2-3x inflated by verifier-evaluator lineage; if our I2 uses same-family Qwen3-Omni to generate AND score, our measured rho is at risk of the same inflation — a methodological KILL-RISK to I2's evaluation VALIDITY unless we enforce decorrelation / cross-family evaluation. I3: no-threat (no abstention). I4: no-threat on supply, but the lineage-inflation is a supply/identity concern feeding our decorrelation constraint.

families.saturation_note: The TEXT half of this family is saturated: Gao 2023 fixes the overoptimization curve shape and the d=sqrt(KL) budget; Snell 2024 fixes difficulty-conditional compute-optimal test-time scaling; Khalaf 2025 proves the BoN peak-then-decline is inevitable and gives an optimal inference-time hedge (HedgeTune). The SPEECH half is saturating fast and now covers each of our identity candidates: MBR-ASR (2510.19471) occupies I1's label-free N-best selection on the exact tasks we hold (LibriSpeech/CoVoST2/FLEURS) — but realizes only ~31% of oracle headroom on clean LibriSpeech (0.042->0.033 vs oracle 0.013) and less under noise, so it CONFIRMS rather than consumes the headroom; READ (2606.04680) occupies I2's audio-grounded training-free selection via a frozen speech model's likelihood (20% rel WERR, strongest under noise) and is the single strongest threat to I2; the auditory-cognition TTC paper (2503.23395) demonstrates I1/I2-style selection on frozen audio LLMs that see audio (+36% to +150% rel) but only on a bespoke 10-person DB with a large external GPT-4o judge; HyPoradise (2309.15701) sets a TRAINED beat-the-selection-oracle upper bound (CHiME-4 6.6 < o_nb 9.1) that bounds how much a training-free selector concedes; and the TTS-BoN paper (2607.08256) shows the audio-verifier's apparent headroom recovery is 2-3x inflated by verifier-evaluator lineage — a direct methodological kill-risk to our same-family Qwen3-Omni-generate-and-score design. Net: the raw ideas 'BoN/MBR/verifier selection on speech' and 'audio-grounded reference-free scoring' are already published; what remains genuinely unclaimed is (a) oracle-headroom REALIZATION RATE (rho) as the primary object, (b) SUPPLY-stratified headroom H(c) (bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval), (c) explicit Goodhart-breakpoint ABSTENTION on speech with a verifiable reward, and (d) verifier-evaluator DECORRELATION as an enforced constraint rather than an uncontrolled confound.

papers.title: Explicit Word Error Minimization in N-Best List Rescoring
papers.task: ASR N-best rescoring by minimizing expected word error (the seminal 'MAP does not minimize WER' argument)
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam/N-best from a SINGLE ASR system, with combined acoustic+LM scores used to estimate hypothesis posteriors (beam-lattice + LM); NOT bare temperature sampling
papers.sees_audio: No — reranks over N-best text + their precomputed acoustic/LM scores; does not re-listen to the waveform
papers.gold_at_train: None used to train a model; an LM/scaling weight may be tuned on a dev set with references
papers.training_required: No — it is an inference-time decoding rule (a dev-tuned posterior-scaling constant aside)
papers.scorer_inputs: N-best hypotheses, their posterior probabilities (from acoustic+LM scores), and pairwise word-level edit distance among hypotheses
papers.selection_operator: argmin over N-best of expected word error: H* = argmin_H sum_{H'} P(H') * WER(H,H') — i.e. MBR with word-error loss over an N-best pool
papers.comparators: MAP / 1-best maximum-likelihood decoding
papers.equal_budget: Fixed N-best size (hundreds); no per-candidate compute-budget control vs a competing selector
papers.datasets_used: SRI Hub-5 conversational telephone speech (Switchboard / CallHome)
papers.eval_protocol: WER on held-out eval, single system
papers.headroom_evidence: Reports modest but real WER reductions over MAP (~fractional-to-~1% absolute in the seminal setting); establishes that MAP leaves the N-best word-error oracle largely unrealized, but the method itself captures only a small slice of it
papers.failure_modes: Gains small; entirely dependent on posterior calibration of the N-best; degenerates when N-best posteriors are poorly estimated
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: This IS our I1 mechanism (label-free N-best selector minimizing expected WER over a frozen pool), 28 years early. Deltas: supply is single-system N-best+LM (not bare-omni K-sampling), scorer is text-only edit distance (no audio), no supply stratification, no abstention, no realization-rate analysis.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL already-done (novelty) — the label-free expected-WER selector over a frozen pool is precisely this 1997 method; I1 cannot claim mechanism novelty, only realization-rate/supply framing. I2: no-threat (text-only, sees no audio). I3: no-threat (no abstention/Goodhart). I4: no-threat (single supply, no stratification).

papers.title: Minimum Bayes-Risk Automatic Speech Recognition
papers.task: MBR ASR decoding via A* search over word lattices / N-best under a task loss (Levenshtein/WER)
papers.candidate_source_supply: word lattices from a conventional (beam) ASR system; posteriors from the lattice, LM baked in (beam-lattice + LM)
papers.sees_audio: No — operates on lattice posteriors, no re-listening
papers.gold_at_train: None
papers.training_required: No — decoding rule (A* / N-best MBR)
papers.scorer_inputs: lattice/N-best hypotheses, their posterior probabilities, and Levenshtein loss between hypotheses
papers.selection_operator: W* = argmin_W sum_{W'} P(W'|A) L(W,W') — canonical MBR (this is exactly our pairwise-MBR comparator)
papers.comparators: MAP decoder
papers.equal_budget: Fixed lattice; no per-candidate budget control
papers.datasets_used: Switchboard (SWB) conversational telephone speech
papers.eval_protocol: WER, single system; efficient A*/N-best approximations to the intractable exact MBR
papers.headroom_evidence: Modest, consistent WER reduction over MAP on Switchboard (reported ~0.3-1.0% absolute range at ~38-42% WER operating point); realizes a small fraction of the lattice/N-best oracle
papers.failure_modes: Small gains; exact MBR prohibitively expensive -> approximations; gain bounded by posterior quality; large residual to oracle
