papers.candidate_source_supply: 1-best outputs from MULTIPLE distinct ASR systems (cross-system diversity), optionally with per-system confidence; a DIFFERENT, more expensive supply than intra-model N-best sampling
papers.sees_audio: No — votes over aligned text (+ optional confidence scores)
papers.gold_at_train: None (voting/confidence thresholds may be tuned on dev)
papers.training_required: No — voting thresholds dev-tuned
papers.scorer_inputs: word-transition / confusion network of the aligned 1-bests; per-slot word frequency-of-occurrence and optional confidence
papers.selection_operator: per-slot majority / confidence-weighted voting over the aligned network
papers.comparators: best individual system
papers.equal_budget: No — requires several independent systems; not a matched-K comparison

papers.eval_protocol: WER; combines 5+ systems

papers.task: Consensus decoding — collapse a word lattice into a confusion network and pick the max-posterior word per slot (per-position WER minimization)
papers.candidate_source_supply: word lattice from a SINGLE ASR system -> confusion network (beam-lattice + LM); also extended to multi-system confusion-network combination
papers.sees_audio: No
papers.gold_at_train: None
papers.training_required: No
papers.scorer_inputs: confusion network with per-slot word posteriors derived from the lattice
papers.selection_operator: per-slot argmax word posterior (consensus) — a per-position MBR approximation to full-sequence MBR
papers.comparators: MAP / Viterbi lattice baseline; also enables confidence estimation and system combination
papers.equal_budget: Fixed lattice
papers.datasets_used: Switchboard: Set I MAP 38.5% -> Consensus 37.3% (-1.2% abs); Set II MAP 42.9% -> 41.6% (-1.3% abs), significant p<0.0001; multi-system consensus ~3-6% relative
papers.eval_protocol: WER with significance testing; single- and multi-system

papers.title: Re-evaluating Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding for Automatic Speech Recognition
papers.task: MBR decoding for modern end-to-end ASR AND speech translation over sampled hypothesis pools from frozen sequence-to-sequence models
papers.candidate_source_supply: BARE-MODEL temperature SAMPLING from frozen Whisper-small/medium/large-v3, distil-large-v3.5, S2T, SeamlessM4T-v2, Kotoba-Whisper; N = 4,8,16,32,64 samples — this is EXACTLY our bare-model K-pool supply
papers.sees_audio: No at scoring time — MBR utility is computed between TEXT hypotheses (BLEU/BLEURT/SentBERT); audio enters only through the sampling model
papers.gold_at_train: None
papers.training_required: No — pure inference-time over frozen models
papers.scorer_inputs: pairwise text-similarity utility (BLEU primary; BLEURT, SentBERT) among the N sampled hypotheses. Critically, they DELIBERATELY DO NOT use WER/CER as the utility 'because MBR decoding is known to inflate the score'
papers.selection_operator: h* = argmax_h sum_{h'} u(h,h') over the sampled pool — MBR consensus
papers.comparators: beam search (B=1, B=20) and oracle best-of-N (N=64)
papers.equal_budget: YES — compares beam vs MBR at matched sample budget and reports an N-scaling curve (N=4..64)
papers.datasets_used: English ASR: LibriSpeech(clean), AMI-IHM, VoxPopuli, CommonVoice-v8; Japanese ASR: ReazonSpeech, JSUT, CommonVoice; ST: CoVoST2 (Ja-En/En-Ja), FLEURS (Ja-En/En-Ja)

papers.code_available: Yes — GitHub link in the abstract
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: CLOSEST prior work to I1 on our exact substrate: MBR over bare-sampled frozen speech/ST-model K-pools, equal-N, LibriSpeech + CoVoST2 + FLEURS, oracle headroom reported. papers.title: Read What You Hear: Reference-Free Hypotheses Evaluation with Acoustic Discrepancy (READ)
papers.task: Reference-free, AUDIO-GROUNDED ASR N-best hypothesis evaluation/selection (and segment-level combination) via acoustic discrepancy between speech and each text hypothesis
papers.candidate_source_supply: N-best (N=5) from an ASR system (beam/N-best supply); the scorer re-listens to the audio
papers.sees_audio: YES — computes the conditional likelihood of discrete speech tokens given each text hypothesis using a frozen auto-regressive TTS model, producing a frame-level acoustic-discrepancy score between the waveform and each hypothesis
papers.gold_at_train: None
papers.training_required: No — frozen CosyVoice2 TTS, 'no additional training on the involved datasets/ASR systems'
papers.scorer_inputs: raw audio (as discrete speech tokens) + each text hypothesis -> P(speech tokens | text) = acoustic-discrepancy score (lower = hypothesis better explains the audio)
papers.selection_operator: argmin acoustic-discrepancy over the N-best (select the hypothesis that best reconstructs the audio); plus a segment-level combination variant
papers.comparators: 1-best baseline, ROVER, LM rescoring; oracle N-best
papers.equal_budget: N=5 fixed
papers.datasets_used: LibriSpeech test-clean (1st-best 2.06% -> READ 1.91%, oracle 1.15%), test-other (3.66 -> 3.48, oracle 2.15), VCTK-noisy (7.41 -> 7.19, oracle 6.14), SWBD-test (15.02 -> 11.93, oracle 10.51), SPGISpeech (4.24 -> 3.33, oracle 2.15)
papers.eval_protocol: WER at N=5 vs ROVER / LM rescoring / oracle
papers.headroom_evidence: Realizes partial oracle headroom: test-clean ~16% ((2.06-1.91)/(2.06-1.15)), test-other ~14%, SWBD large (~(15.02-11.93)/(15.02-10.51)=68%); paper's headline 'headroom' figures (~42-50% for some rows) refer to segment-level combination configs and should be treated as approximate. Substantial residual to oracle in all cases.
papers.failure_modes: Depends on the frozen TTS model's domain/coverage; N=5 only; small gains on clean read speech, large on conversational/mismatched (SWBD); no abstention; TTS-likelihood is a proxy, not a comprehension signal
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: CLOSEST prior work to I2: a training-free, AUDIO-GROUNDED, frozen-model selector over ASR N-best that beats 1-best/ROVER. Deltas: (a) signal is generative TTS acoustic-likelihood P(speech|text), NOT an omni-MLLM comprehension/semantic signal (our I2 uses frozen omni-native signals from Qwen3-Omni); (b) N=5 beam N-best, not bare-omni K-sampling; (c) no supply stratification; (d) no abstention/Goodhart; (e) realizes only ~14-68% of oracle -> ρ framing survives.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL (another label-free N-best selector, but its edge is audio -> really an I2 paper). I2: STRONG PARTIAL already-done — a training-free, audio-grounded, frozen-model N-best selector EXISTS and beats 1-best/ROVER on LibriSpeech/SWBD; the CONCEPT of I2 is done. BUT the mechanism differs (TTS-reconstruction likelihood vs omni-native understanding signal), supply differs (beam N-best vs bare omni K-pool), no supply stratification, and only partial headroom realized -> I2's specific omni-signal + realization-rate + supply-stratification claims remain open. I3: no-threat. I4: no-threat.

papers.title: HyPoradise: An Open Baseline for Generative Speech Recognition with Large Language Models
papers.task: LLM generative error correction (hypotheses-to-transcription, H2T) — rewrite the transcript from the N-best list rather than select from it
papers.candidate_source_supply: N-best (N=5) from a frozen ASR system (Whisper etc.); the LLM ingests the whole N-best text list (beam N-best supply)
papers.sees_audio: No — text-only N-best fed to the LLM; no audio
papers.gold_at_train: YES — LoRA-fine-tuned on 334K hypotheses-transcription pairs (needs gold transcripts to train the corrector)
papers.training_required: YES — LoRA fine-tuning of the LLM (H2T-LoRA). This is the decisive contrast with our training-FREE stance
papers.scorer_inputs: N-best text list -> LLM GENERATES a corrected transcript (free-form), not a scored selection
papers.selection_operator: generative (free-form output) — can emit tokens/words OUTSIDE the pool; NOT argmax over the pool
papers.comparators: N-best reranking oracle (o_nb, the ceiling for selection methods), compositional oracle (o_cp), LM rescoring
papers.eval_protocol: WER vs the N-best reranking oracle o_nb
papers.headroom_evidence: KEY BOUNDARY RESULT: GER SURPASSES the N-best reranking oracle o_nb on WSJ (2.2<4.1), ATIS (1.7<5.2), CHiME-4 (6.6<9.1), LRS2 (6.6<6.9) — i.e. the SELECTION oracle that all selectors (I1/I2) target is NOT the true ceiling; generation eats past it. But it FAILS to beat o_nb on SwitchBoard (14.1>12.6) and is marginal on CommonVoice (11.0 vs 11.4)
papers.failure_modes: Requires LoRA training + gold pairs; regresses on conversational/accented speech (SwitchBoard, CORAAL); can hallucinate; not a selection method
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: BOUNDARY / adjacent family (generative, TRAINED, text-only). It bounds I1's value proposition: the N-best oracle ceiling our selectors chase can be exceeded by a TRAINED generator. But it needs LoRA + gold transcripts, so it does NOT threaten training-free selection directly — it reframes the ceiling and forces I1 to justify 'why select training-free instead of train-and-generate'.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL / BOUNDARY — proves the reranking oracle is not the ultimate ceiling (GER beats o_nb on 4+ sets), so I1's 'realize the oracle headroom' has a higher ceiling above it; but GER requires training + gold, so it does NOT kill training-free label-free selection — I1 must argue the training-free/label-free advantage and target the ρ gap below o_nb. I2: no-threat (text-only, no audio). I3: no-threat. I4: no-threat.

papers.title: It's MBR All the Way Down: Modern Generation Techniques Through the Lens of Minimum Bayes Risk
papers.task: Theoretical unification — shows self-consistency, majority voting, N-best reranking, and other inference-time selection methods are special cases of MBR decoding
papers.candidate_source_supply: general sampled pools from (text) LLMs — bare-model sampling; task-agnostic framing
papers.sees_audio: No
papers.gold_at_train: None
papers.training_required: No — inference-time only ('several-point improvements across metrics without any additional data or training')
papers.scorer_inputs: pairwise utility among sampled candidates; with exact-match utility this reduces to count-based majority voting / self-consistency
papers.selection_operator: MBR argmax; PROVES majority-vote and self-consistency = MBR with exact-match utility (and reranking = MBR with a reference-free utility)
papers.comparators: greedy, sampling, reranking, self-consistency
papers.equal_budget: Conceptual; discusses sample-count / inference-cost tradeoff
papers.datasets_used: MT, summarization, reasoning (text) — NOT ASR/speech
papers.eval_protocol: reliable several-point metric gains across tasks (no ASR numbers)
papers.headroom_evidence: Frames the whole family; 'reliable several-point improvements across metrics for a wide variety of tasks without training' — but no oracle-headroom or realization-rate analysis
papers.failure_modes: Utility-metric dependence; needs sample diversity; degenerates with a poor/degenerate utility (e.g. exact-match on continuous outputs)
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: The conceptual bridge that fixes our NOVELTY boundary: our I1 with an exact-match reward callable = MBR-exact-match = majority voting / self-consistency; our pairwise-MBR baseline = MBR with a text utility. The label-free-selection MECHANISM is a named, unified, pre-existing idea. Deltas: no audio, no speech, no supply stratification, no abstention, no realization-rate object.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: STRONG on NOVELTY — explicitly names and unifies our mechanism (label-free pool selection = MBR; exact-match reward = majority vote = self-consistency). I1 cannot be positioned as 'we invented label-free selection'; the contribution must be supply-stratification / audio-grounding / realization-rate / abstention. I2: no-threat (no audio). I3: no-threat. I4: no-threat.

families.saturation_note: The classic ASR-selection mechanisms of this family are 25+ years old and MECHANISM-SATURATED for text-only, single-metric selection over lattice/N-best/multi-system supply: expected-WER N-best rescoring (Stolcke 1997), MBR/A*-over-lattices (Goel-Byrne 2000), confusion-network consensus (Mangu 2000), and multi-system voting (ROVER 1997) all instantiate 'pick the pool member minimizing expected loss / max word posterior'. Bertsch 2023 closes the loop by proving that self-consistency and majority voting are just MBR with exact-match utility — i.e. a label-free selector over a frozen K-pool (our I1) IS MBR, a named 1997-2000 idea. Modern descendants have re-validated the mechanism on our exact substrate: Re-evaluating-MBR (2025) runs MBR over BARE-SAMPLED frozen Whisper/Seamless K-pools at equal N (4-64) on LibriSpeech/CoVoST2/FLEURS and beats beam; READ (2026) is a training-free, AUDIO-GROUNDED frozen-model N-best selector on LibriSpeech/SWBD. So 'training-free label-free selection over a frozen speech/omni K-pool' — including an audio-grounded variant — is largely DONE as a concept. What is NOT saturated and where our identity must live: (1) every method here realizes only ~15-45% of measured oracle headroom (Re-evaluating-MBR ~30-45% on LS-clean; READ ~14-16% on LS-clean, ~68% on SWBD; classics ~1.2-1.3% abs of a much larger N-best oracle) — the realization-rate ρ gap is real, large, and unclosed, and NO paper treats ρ as the primary object; (2) none stratify oracle headroom by capability-supply c (bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval) — I4 is untouched; (3) READ's audio signal is a generative TTS acoustic-likelihood P(speech|text), NOT an omni-MLLM comprehension signal — I2's specific omni-native mechanism is open; (4) none add abstention / Goodhart-breakpoint detection — I3 is untouched; (5) WER-as-utility is a KNOWN degeneracy (Re-evaluating-MBR explicitly refuses WER/CER utility 'because MBR is known to inflate the score'), so a naive verifiable-reward MBR selector is fragile and the family offers no principled fix beyond swapping to neural text metrics.
gaps: Supply-conditionality is entirely absent: no paper in this family varies the candidate-generation supply (bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval) and measures oracle headroom H(c) or realization as a function of supply — the classics assume beam/lattice/multi-system supply, and even the 2025 re-eval uses only a single bare-sampling supply. I4 (supply-stratified headroom realization) is completely uncovered.

No omni-MLLM-native audio-understanding signal is used as the selection utility. Classics use text-derived posteriors (no audio at scoring time); READ 2026 is audio-grounded but via a frozen TTS acoustic-likelihood P(speech tokens|text), not a comprehension/semantic signal from a frozen omni model. I2's specific mechanism (frozen omni-native signals from Qwen3-Omni) is untested.
No abstention, no constrained/cross-task selection, and no Goodhart-breakpoint detection anywhere in the family — selection is always unconditional argmin/argmax. I3 is entirely uncovered.

Realization rate (fraction of oracle headroom captured) is reported only incidentally and never optimized as the target object; no method asks 'why is ~55-85% of the oracle headroom left on the table and how do we close it?' — our ρ framing is novel-as-object even though the selectors themselves are old.

Equal-budget bare-sampling comparison appears ONLY in the 2025 re-eval; classic MBR/ROVER/CN work compares against MAP/best-single-system at fixed lattice/system count, never controlling per-candidate compute budget K against a selector prototype.

Noise / SNR degradation of the realization rate is unstudied — classic work is almost all clean-channel or conversational-telephone (Switchboard/Hub-5); none maps how ρ collapses from clean to snr5 the way our C-ASR-V2 battery does (rho_greedy ~42% clean -> ~24% snr5).

The family's ceiling is the N-best/reranking ORACLE, but HyPoradise 2023 shows GENERATIVE correction can surpass that ceiling — yet only with LoRA training + gold transcripts; the family has no training-free way to exceed the selection oracle, and no analysis of when selection (our stance) is preferable to trained generation.

Utility-function fragility (WER-as-reward degeneracy) is acknowledged but unsolved for verifiable-reward settings; no principled abstaining/robust selector that keeps a WER/exact-match reward yet avoids MBR score-inflation.

families.family: LLM N-best rescoring, revision and generation (HypR / ProGRes / HyPoradise GEC lineage)

papers.title: HypR: A comprehensive study for ASR hypothesis revising with a reference corpus
papers.task: ASR hypothesis revising benchmark that explicitly separates the family into two sub-tasks: N-best RERANKING (select lowest-WER candidate) vs ERROR CORRECTION (detect+rewrite errors). Provides 50 hypotheses/utterance (experiments use top-10) plus released ASR checkpoints.
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam-lattice: beam-search N-best, with and without shallow-fusion of an extra n-gram/neural LM. NOT sampling-based, NOT retrieval-augmented.
papers.sees_audio: No for almost all methods (text-only reranking over hypotheses). Exception: BERT-align/sem-style comparators that inject acoustic features. LLM zero-shot methods are text-only.
papers.gold_at_train: Yes for supervised rerankers/correctors (PBERT, RescoreBERT, BERT variants, BART) — trained on hyp/reference pairs. LLM prompt methods use no training.
papers.gold_at_test: No (reference used only to compute WER, not fed to the selector).
papers.training_required: Mixed: reranking (PBERT/RescoreBERT/BERT) and correction (BART) are SUPERVISED fine-tuned; LLM (e.g., chatGPT/LLaMA) methods are zero-shot/training-free prompt-based.
papers.scorer_inputs: Text hypotheses (+ optional LM scores) for reranking; hypothesis text for correction. No verifiable-reward callable — models learn/prompt a scorer, not a WER/EM oracle.
papers.selection_operator: Reranking arm = argmin over N-best of a learned/LM score (pure SELECTION, output constrained to the pool). Correction arm = free rewriting (unconstrained generation).
papers.comparators: Top-1 baseline, N-best oracle (lower bound), supervised rerankers (PBERT/RescoreBERT), correction models (BART), LLM zero-shot; both w/ and w/o LM.
papers.equal_budget: No equal-K training-free protocol; compares heterogeneous supervised vs zero-shot methods at fixed top-10 N-best.
papers.datasets_used: AISHELL-1, TED-LIUM 2, LibriSpeech (clean + other). English + Mandarin.
papers.eval_protocol: WER/CER on dev+test; reports Top-1 vs Oracle headroom per corpus. Standardized splits with released checkpoints for reproducibility.
papers.headroom_evidence: Oracle (top-10) headroom is small and corpus-dependent: LibriSpeech-clean test 2.55->1.15 (1.40 abs); LibriSpeech-other test 7.12->4.48 (2.64 abs); TED-LIUM2 test 12.07->8.55 (3.52 abs); AISHELL-1 test 8.33->4.74 (3.59 abs, CER); dev headrooms 2.16-3.77 abs. Realized fraction by reranking methods is a minority of this gap; correction methods can exceed oracle by rewriting.
papers.failure_modes: Reranking capped by oracle; supervised methods need in-domain hyp/ref pairs; correction methods hallucinate (insert unspoken tokens). Small absolute headroom limits achievable gain.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Same selection-vs-rewriting dichotomy and oracle-headroom framing we use, BUT: beam-lattice supply (not multi-seed sampling), text-only, ASR-only, rerankers are supervised, no verifiable-reward selector, no supply stratification, no abstention. Our I1/I2 = training-free selection over SAMPLED omni K-pools scored by a verifiable reward.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL THREAT — establishes N-best reranking=selection as a mature task and quantifies small oracle headroom (1.4-3.6 abs WER), but its rerankers are SUPERVISED so it does not preempt a training-free label-free selector; not killed. I2: NO THREAT — reranking is text-only; audio-grounded training-free selection unaddressed. I3: NO THREAT — no constraint/abstention/Goodhart study. I4: NO THREAT — single beam-lattice supply, never supply-stratified.

papers.title: ProGRes: Prompted Generative Rescoring on ASR n-Best
papers.task: Zero-shot LLM rescoring that first EXPANDS the N-best by prompting an instruction-tuned LLM to generate new hypotheses, then rescores the enlarged pool by combining ASR confidence + LLM sequence score (interpolation weight alpha tuned on dev).
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam-lattice base (n=10 ASR1, n=20 ASR2) AUGMENTED by +LM generation supply (LLM-prompted new hypotheses). This is a hybrid beam + prompt-generation supply.
papers.sees_audio: No — text-only. LLMs receive transcript hypotheses only; audio never enters the LLM (ASR confidence is the only acoustic signal, as a scalar).
papers.gold_at_train: N/A — no training.
papers.gold_at_test: No (reference only for WER; dev used to tune alpha).
papers.training_required: None — fully zero-shot/training-free (frozen LLMs + frozen ASR).
papers.scorer_inputs: ASR confidence score + LLM (Llama-3 8B) sequence log-prob over hypothesis text; linear interpolation. No WER/EM reward callable.
papers.selection_operator: argmax over EXPANDED pool of alpha*conf + (1-alpha)*LLM-score. Selection, but over a pool the LLM has grown by generation (so output can be a newly-generated string, not strictly a member of the original beam N-best).
papers.comparators: Prompt-only, LLM-rescoring-only, ProGRes (combined), Oracle. Generators compared: Llama-3-Instruct, GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4-Turbo.
papers.equal_budget: Partial — fixed base N-best, but pool size changes after LLM expansion; no equal-K parity vs a pure selector.
papers.datasets_used: CommonVoice (English, ~16.3k test utts); ASR1 = SPGISpeech/CommonVoice-trained Conformer, ASR2 = CommonVoice 16.1 WavLM-CTC (SpeechBrain).
papers.eval_protocol: WER on CommonVoice; reports baseline WER, ProGRes WER, and oracle WER of expanded pool; relative WER improvement.
papers.headroom_evidence: LLM expansion barely moves the oracle: ASR1 oracle 38.38->36.17, ASR2 oracle 6.82->5.48. Realized: ASR1 42.94->40.84 (4.9% rel); ASR2 12.38->9.32 (24.7% rel). So it realizes a modest slice of headroom via a text-only frozen LLM; the oracle itself stays largely fixed.
papers.failure_modes: Text-only ceiling; helps high-WER ASR much more than low-WER ASR (4.9% vs 24.7% rel); alpha must be dev-tuned; generation can add wrong hypotheses.
papers.code_available: Not confirmed in search (SpeechBrain-based recipe implied; no verified public repo).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: This is the CLOSEST training-free precedent to I1: frozen-LLM zero-shot rescoring of ASR N-best combining confidence + LLM score. Deltas: text-only (no audio grounding => I2 open), beam+prompt supply (not multi-seed sampling), ASR-only, no verifiable-reward scorer (uses LLM log-prob not WER/EM oracle), no supply stratification, no abstention.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: STRONGEST THREAT in family but NOT a kill — a training-free frozen-LLM selector over ASR N-best already exists and realizes 4.9-24.7% rel WER; however it is text-only, uses LLM-logprob (not a verifiable reward), and does NOT report the oracle-realization fraction rho we target, and never touches omni/multitask pools. I2: NO THREAT — no audio grounding. I3: NO THREAT — no constraint/abstention/breakpoint. I4: NO THREAT — no supply stratification (its LLM-expansion is a single fixed supply mode).

papers.title: Whispering LLaMA: A Cross-Modal Generative Error Correction Framework for Speech Recognition
papers.task: Cross-modal generative error correction: fuse Whisper acoustic encoder features into a LLaMA decoder (via cross-attention adapters) to rewrite the transcript from the N-best. Audio-grounded rewriting, not selection.
papers.candidate_source_supply: SAMPLING supply — top-k=200, temperature 0.7-0.8 from Whisper-Tiny, filtered to 15-best. This is the ONE family paper whose candidate supply matches our multi-sample generation regime.
papers.sees_audio: YES — Whisper-Large-V2 (1.55B) encoder acoustic features fused into LLaMA-7B decoder. The core novelty is injecting audio into the LLM (WERR 28.83%->37.66% attributed to the acoustic fusion).
papers.gold_at_train: Yes — trains residual/cross-attn adapters on hyp+audio->reference pairs.
papers.training_required: YES — parameter-efficient fine-tuning (residual adapters, 4.89M-26.4M trainable params; LLaMA-7B/Whisper frozen). Not training-free.
papers.scorer_inputs: Audio features + N-best text -> generated transcript (no explicit scorer; end-to-end trained decoder).
papers.selection_operator: None (free generation). Output is a rewritten string, not a pool member.
papers.comparators: N-best oracle, text-only correction baselines, three adapter sizes (WL_S/M/L).
papers.equal_budget: No — training-based; compared against text-only correction and oracle, not against an equal-K training-free selector.
papers.datasets_used: ATIS, GigaSpeech subsets (Entertainment GSE, People&Blogs GSP, Sci&Tech GSSS/GSSM). English.
papers.eval_protocol: WER + WERR relative to N-best oracle. Reports oracle 21.64 avg -> best model 13.48 avg (37.66% WERR).
papers.headroom_evidence: Best model (WL_M) beats the N-best oracle: avg oracle 21.64 vs WL_M 13.48 (37.66% relative to oracle), i.e., audio-grounded rewriting eats and EXCEEDS the selection oracle. But this requires trained adapters.
papers.failure_modes: Needs paired training data + audio; adapter tuning cost; rewriting can hallucinate; gains depend on adapter size.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: CLOSEST audio-grounded precedent to I2 AND closest supply match (multi-sample top-k) to our K-pools. But it TRAINS cross-modal adapters and REWRITES; ours is training-free SELECTION using frozen omni-native signals. It shows audio-grounding beats the selection oracle only WITH training.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: NO THREAT (rewriting, not label-free selection). I2: PARTIAL THREAT — proves audio-grounding beats the N-best oracle (37.66% WERR), the exact capability I2 wants, BUT requires trained cross-modal adapters, so it does NOT preempt a TRAINING-FREE audio-grounded selector; not killed and actually marks the training-free version as open whitespace. I3: NO THREAT. I4: NO THREAT — single sampling supply, no stratification.

papers.title: ASR Error Correction using Large Language Models (Ma et al., Cambridge)
papers.task: Zero-shot (GPT-3.5/4) and fine-tuned (T5) ASR error correction, with an explicit study of CONSTRAINED vs UNCONSTRAINED decoding: unconstrained free rewrite, N-best-constrained, closest-hypothesis, and lattice-constrained correction.
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam-lattice — Conformer-Transducer and Whisper 5-best/10-best; also a full lattice variant. Text-only.
papers.sees_audio: No — 'requires only the decoding hypotheses and reference data'; audio not used by the corrector.
papers.gold_at_train: For T5 fine-tuned arm yes; for GPT zero-shot arm no.
papers.training_required: Mixed — GPT-3.5/GPT-4 arms are zero-shot/training-free; T5 arm is fine-tuned.
papers.scorer_inputs: N-best text (+ lattice) -> corrected text; the CONSTRAINED variants restrict output to the N-best pool or the closest hypothesis (a selection-like constraint).
papers.selection_operator: Closest-hypothesis / N-best-constrained = SELECTION-restricted decoding (output must be a pool member); unconstrained = free generation. Directly contrasts the two.
papers.comparators: Baseline, 10-best T5 (uncon/constr/lattice), GPT-3.5 (closest), GPT-4 (uncon), oracle.
papers.equal_budget: Partial — fixed 5/10-best across methods; contrasts constrained vs unconstrained at equal N, closest to an equal-budget lens.
papers.datasets_used: LibriSpeech (clean+other), TED-LIUM3, Artie Bias Corpus; internal MGB-3, Linguaskill.
papers.eval_protocol: WER; reports oracle WER reduction (Transducer 10-best oracle 38.4% WERR on test_other; Whisper 10-best 35.8%), plus method WERs.
papers.headroom_evidence: Realizes a slice, capped by oracle: Transducer other 6.90 baseline -> T5 uncon 6.37 / constr 6.15 / lattice 6.10; GPT-4 uncon 5.79; oracle ~4.25 (10-best). Whisper other 7.37 -> T5 uncon 6.39 (constr 6.69, i.e., constraint HURT Whisper by 0.30). Explicitly: correction 'remains bounded by the oracle.'
papers.failure_modes: Unconstrained GPT rewriting can add errors (constraint helps Transducer +0.22 but hurts Whisper -0.30 => constraint value is system-dependent); zero-shot GPT weaker than fine-tuned T5 in some settings; bounded by oracle.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: CLOSEST precedent to I3: it studies constrained (N-best/closest) vs unconstrained decoding, i.e., the constraint idea, and shows unconstrained rewriting hallucinates. Deltas: text-only, ASR-only, beam supply, NO abstention and NO explicit Goodhart-breakpoint detector, no verifiable-reward selector, no cross-task, no supply stratification.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL THREAT — 'closest-hypothesis' constrained GPT is a training-free selection-like operator over N-best; but text-only, beam supply, does not report rho oracle-realization; not killed. I2: NO THREAT (text-only). I3: STRONGEST THREAT to I3 framing — already contrasts constrained vs unconstrained and documents hallucination when unconstrained (constraint swing +0.22/-0.30 WER), BUT provides NO abstention and NO breakpoint DETECTOR; I3's explicit Goodhart-breakpoint/abstaining selector is unaddressed => not killed. I4: NO THREAT — no supply stratification.

papers.title: HyPoradise: An Open Baseline for Generative Speech Recognition with Large Language Models
papers.task: Generative error correction (H2T = hypotheses-to-transcript) benchmark: LLM generates the reference from the N-best list, explicitly positioned as surpassing the re-ranking (selection) upper bound. 316k+ hyp/transcript pairs.
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam-lattice — top-5 highest-probability hypotheses from each ASR (Whisper/Conformer). Text-only.
papers.sees_audio: No — LLM sees only the N-best text.
papers.gold_at_train: Yes — H2T-LoRA/H2T-ft trained on hyp/ref pairs.
papers.training_required: YES — H2T-LoRA fine-tunes LLaMA-13B (LoRA); H2T-ft fine-tunes T5. (Also reports in-context/zero-shot as weaker baselines.)
papers.scorer_inputs: N-best text -> generated transcript; no verifiable-reward scorer.
papers.selection_operator: None — free generation (rewriting), the whole point being to escape the selection oracle.
papers.comparators: Baseline top-1, LM-rerank, H2T-ft (T5), H2T-LoRA (LLaMA), oracle o_nb (selection upper bound) and o_cp (compositional/token-level upper bound).
papers.equal_budget: No — training-based vs oracle; fixed top-5.
papers.datasets_used: WSJ, ATIS, CHiME-4, Tedlium-3, CommonVoice-accent, SwitchBoard, LRS2, CORAAL.
papers.eval_protocol: WER; reports baseline, method, and BOTH oracle bounds o_nb (best N-best member) and o_cp (best token-composition).
papers.headroom_evidence: KEY: trained GER BEATS the selection oracle o_nb on multiple sets — WSJ 4.5 base / o_nb 4.1 / LoRA 2.2; CHiME-4 11.1 / o_nb 9.1 / LoRA 6.6; CommonVoice 14.8 / o_nb 11.4 / LoRA 11.0; CORAAL 21.4 / o_nb 21.8 / LoRA 19.2. (Does NOT beat o_nb on Tedlium-3 4.6 vs 3.0 or SwitchBoard 14.1 vs 12.6.) The compositional oracle o_cp (0.7-10.7) is far below o_nb, showing large token-level headroom rewriting can chase.
papers.failure_modes: Requires LoRA fine-tuning on in-domain pairs; text-only; does not beat o_nb on all sets; rewriting risks hallucination on rare entities.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: This is the paper that most directly PRESSURES our oracle-headroom story: it demonstrates the selection oracle o_nb is NOT the true ceiling — a TRAINED generative LLM surpasses it. Delta: it needs LoRA fine-tuning + in-domain pairs; ours is training-free. For a training-free SELECTOR, o_nb best-of-N remains the ceiling, which HyPoradise itself does not refute in the zero-shot regime.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: THREAT to FRAMING (not method) — proves oracle best-of-N is beatable, so 'oracle = ceiling' only holds for TRAINING-FREE selection; must be stated carefully. Not a method kill: requires supervised LoRA. I2: NO THREAT (text-only). I3: NO THREAT — introduces o_cp compositional bound but no constraint/abstention selector. I4: NO THREAT — single beam supply, no stratification; but its o_nb vs o_cp gap is exactly the kind of supply/ceiling analysis I4 should generalize.

papers.title: RobustGER: Large Language Models are Efficient Learners of Noise-Robust Speech Recognition
papers.task: Noise-robust generative error correction: LLM predicts reference from noisy-ASR N-best using a language-space noise embedding distilled from audio (MINE mutual-information distillation). Extends HyPoradise to noisy corpora (Robust HyPoradise, 113k+ pairs).
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam-lattice — N=5 N-best from noisy-condition ASR. Text N-best + a distilled noise embedding.
papers.sees_audio: Partially — audio embeddings from the ASR encoder are used during TRAINING (distilled into language-space noise embedding via MINE); at inference it operates on the learned language-space embedding (no raw audio at test).
papers.gold_at_train: Yes — adapter tuning on noisy hyp/ref pairs + audio distillation.
papers.training_required: YES — LLaMA-Adapter parameter-efficient tuning + audio-distillation module. Not training-free.
papers.scorer_inputs: N-best text + language-space noise embedding -> generated transcript; no verifiable reward.
papers.selection_operator: None — free generation (denoising rewrite).
papers.comparators: Baseline top-1, N-best oracle o_nb, GER (HyPoradise) without noise embedding, in-context learning.
papers.equal_budget: No — training-based; fixed N=5.
papers.datasets_used: CHiME-4, VoiceBank-DEMAND, NOIZEUS, LibriSpeech-FreeSound, RATS (real + simulated noise).
papers.eval_protocol: WER per noisy corpus + overall; reports baseline, RobustGER, and o_nb.
papers.headroom_evidence: Beats o_nb strongly under noise: CHiME-4 test-real 12.6 base / o_nb 10.5 / RobustGER 5.6 (-55.6%); dev-real 10.6 / 9.1 / 4.1 (-61.3%). Overall 12.8 base / o_nb 10.8 / 5.9 (-53.9%). On some sets it stays above o_nb (VB-DEMAND 10.7 vs 8.6; NOIZEUS 12.6 vs 9.2; RATS 43.2 vs 38.8). So trained noise-aware rewriting exceeds the selection oracle in high-noise regimes.
papers.failure_modes: Needs adapter training + paired noisy data + audio distillation; smaller gains at low SNR mismatch (RATS only -5.5%); rewriting hallucination risk.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: DIRECTLY relevant to our snr5 noise battery: LS-FreeSound (LibriSpeech+FreeSound noise) is the analogue of our librispeech test-other+snr5. RobustGER shows audio-informed rewriting beats o_nb under noise, but only WITH adapter training + audio distillation. Ours is training-free selection over noisy sampled K-pools; the training-free realized-headroom rho under noise is exactly what it does not measure.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: NO THREAT (rewriting + trained). I2: PARTIAL THREAT — best audio-informed noisy-ASR result in family and it beats o_nb (-53.9%), the capability I2 wants under noise, BUT requires adapter training + audio distillation, so training-free audio-grounded selection on snr5 pools remains open; not killed. I3: NO THREAT. I4: WEAK RELEVANCE — noise vs clean is a supply/condition axis, but it never stratifies headroom by capability-supply nor abstains.

papers.title: Failing Forward (DARAG): Improving Generative Error Correction for ASR with Synthetic Data and Retrieval Augmentation
papers.task: Retrieval-augmented + synthetic-data generative error correction: retrieve top-k named entities (SentenceBERT) similar to the best hypothesis and add them to the correction prompt; augment training with TTS-synthesized speech. Directly manipulates the CONTEXT/RETRIEVAL supply given to the corrector.
papers.candidate_source_supply: beam N-best (N=5) + RETRIEVAL supply (top-5 retrieved named entities as comma-separated prompt context) + synthetic (TTS) training supply. The one family paper that explicitly adds a +retrieval-context supply arm.
papers.sees_audio: Only via TTS-synthesized speech used to create more training hyp/ref pairs; corrector input at test is text (N-best + retrieved entities).
papers.gold_at_train: Yes — LoRA fine-tune on (augmented) hyp/ref pairs.
papers.gold_at_test: No (retrieved entities are external, not the reference).
papers.training_required: YES — LoRA on LLaMA-2 with data augmentation. Not training-free.
papers.scorer_inputs: N-best text + retrieved NE list -> generated transcript; no verifiable reward.
papers.selection_operator: None — free generation conditioned on retrieved context.
papers.comparators: Baseline top-1, vanilla GER, +synthetic, +retrieval (DARAG), in-domain and OOD.
papers.equal_budget: No — training-based; fixed N=5.
papers.datasets_used: LibriSpeech-960, SPGISpeech, VoxPopuli, GigaSpeech, TED-LIUM.
papers.eval_protocol: WER, in-domain and OOD; reports 8-30% (in-domain) / 10-33% (OOD) rel improvement.
papers.headroom_evidence: Baseline vs DARAG: LibriSpeech 4.6->4.0 (13.0%); VoxPopuli 8.2->6.1 (25.6%); SPGI 8.9->8.0 (10.1%). N-best oracle not explicitly reported (weakness for headroom comparison).
papers.failure_modes: Needs LoRA training + retrieval index + TTS pipeline; retrieval helps entities but adds prompt noise; no oracle reported so realized-fraction unknown; rewriting hallucination.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: CLOSEST precedent to I4's +retrieval supply arm: it changes the CONTEXT supplied to the corrector (retrieved NEs) and measures WER change. Deltas: it adds retrieval to a TRAINED REWRITING model, never STRATIFIES oracle headroom H(c) by supply level (bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval), never measures a training-free selector's realization rho as a function of supply, and reports no oracle bound.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: NO THREAT (trained rewriting). I2: NO THREAT (audio only via TTS training). I3: NO THREAT. I4: PARTIAL THREAT — establishes that adding retrieval-context supply improves GER (10-33% OOD), so 'supply matters' is shown, BUT it does NOT stratify oracle headroom by supply or realize it with a training-free selector, so I4's supply-conditional headroom-realization H(c) analysis is unaddressed; not killed and is clear whitespace.

families.saturation_note: The LLM N-best rescoring/revision/generation family is HEAVILY saturated on ASR word-error-rate error correction, and it has already produced the single most dangerous finding for our headroom narrative: trained generative error correction (HyPoradise LoRA, Whispering-LLaMA adapters, RobustGER adapters) SURPASSES the N-best selection oracle o_nb (e.g., HyPoradise CHiME-4 6.6 vs o_nb 9.1; Whispering-LLaMA 37.66% WERR beyond oracle; RobustGER -53.9% overall beyond o_nb 10.8). So 'oracle best-of-N is the ceiling' is TRUE ONLY for training-free SELECTION, and we must frame our +0.042 oracle-headroom claim strictly within the training-free-selection regime, never as a universal ceiling. HOWEVER the family is NOT saturated where we operate: (1) truly TRAINING-FREE methods are only ProGRes and the Cambridge zero-shot GPT arm, and BOTH are text-only (no audio grounding) and use LLM-logprob rather than a verifiable-reward (WER/EM) scorer; (2) candidate supply is almost always beam-lattice (+optional LM) — only Whispering-LLaMA uses multi-sample top-k sampling like our multi-seed K-pools; (3) EVERYTHING is ASR-WER-centric — none evaluate selection over our omni multitask suite (ST/SER/SLU/spoken-QA/audio-understanding); (4) NONE do supply-stratified headroom realization (I4) and NONE build an abstaining/Goodhart-breakpoint selector (I3). Net: the family threatens the FRAMING of I1's oracle ceiling and marks audio-grounded correction (I2) and retrieval-supply (I4) as achievable-with-training, but it does NOT preempt any training-free, verifiable-reward, omni-multitask, supply-stratified, or abstaining SELECTOR — those are open.
gaps: Training-free vs trained: the strongest family methods (HyPoradise, Whispering-LLaMA, RobustGER, Failing-Forward) all REQUIRE fine-tuning/adapters on in-domain hyp-ref pairs; the only training-free members (ProGRes, Cambridge zero-shot GPT) are text-only and use LLM log-prob, never a verifiable WER/EM reward scorer as the selection operator.

Selection vs rewriting is conflated: the family's headline gains come from REWRITING (free generation) that can hallucinate; pure label-free SELECTION over a fixed pool (our I1) is studied only in HypR's reranking arm and there only with SUPERVISED rerankers.

Candidate supply is almost always beam-lattice (+optional LM). Multi-seed SAMPLING pools (ours) appear only in Whispering-LLaMA; no family paper studies how realized headroom depends on sampling temperature / seeds / N in a training-free selector.

Supply-stratification is absent: no paper measures oracle headroom H(c) as a function of capability-supply (bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval). Failing-Forward adds a retrieval-context arm but never stratifies the oracle or reports realized fraction vs supply (I4 whitespace).

Abstention / Goodhart-breakpoint detection is absent: Cambridge studies constrained vs unconstrained decoding and documents hallucination, but no family paper builds a selector that ABSTAINS or detects a reward-hacking breakpoint (I3 whitespace).

Modality/task coverage: the family is ~100% ASR-WER (plus a little AVSR); none evaluate reference-free/verifiable-reward SELECTION on speech translation (covost2/fleurs-r), SER (crema-d/meld), SLU/intent (slurp/minds14/speech-massive), spoken-QA (spoken-squad/heysquad), or audio-understanding (mmau/mmar/air-bench) — our omni multitask footprint is uncontested.
Equal-budget parity is rarely enforced: comparisons mix heterogeneous supervised and zero-shot methods; no clean equal-K training-free selector-vs-selector protocol exists to benchmark realized rho.

Audio-grounded TRAINING-FREE selection (I2) does not exist in the family: audio helps (Whispering-LLaMA, RobustGER) but only through trained cross-modal fusion/distillation, never as a frozen omni-native signal driving a zero-training selector.

families.family: Multi-verifier, uncertainty, abstention and pessimistic selection at inference time

papers.title: Is Best-of-N the Best of Them? Coverage, Scaling, and Optimality in Inference-Time Alignment (introduces InferenceTimePessimism)
papers.task: Training-free inference-time alignment / selection over language-model generations; math reasoning (GSM8K) and instruction-following (AlpacaEval-2.0).
papers.candidate_source_supply: Bare-model sampling: N i.i.d. draws from a frozen pretrained policy pi_ref, no beam/LM/retrieval. Same supply regime as our K-pools.
papers.sees_audio: No. Text-only LLM outputs.
papers.gold_at_train: No policy training; assumes a pre-existing (possibly RLHF-trained) imperfect reward model r-hat as the only supervision surrogate.
papers.gold_at_test: No test-time gold labels. Selection uses only r-hat; degradation is measured against a separate gold reward/accuracy oracle for analysis.
papers.training_required: Training-free at inference (algorithm is rejection sampling); but assumes an externally-trained reward model exists.
papers.scorer_inputs: Scalar imperfect reward r-hat(prompt, response). No audio, no gold.
papers.selection_operator: InferenceTimePessimism = chi-squared-regularized rejection sampling implementing pessimism-in-face-of-uncertainty; coefficient beta>0 trades reward vs divergence from pi_ref. Contrast: naive Best-of-N = argmax r-hat.
papers.comparators: Naive Best-of-N (BoN) / BoN-Alignment as the primary baseline; pi_ref as floor.
papers.equal_budget: Yes — analysis is explicitly as a function of compute budget N; key result is behavior of both methods at matched N.
papers.datasets_used: GSM8K (reward model OASST as r-hat), AlpacaEval-2.0 (appendix); multiple policies/tasks referenced.
papers.eval_protocol: Sweep N; plot gold accuracy and r-hat vs N. Theory: BoN suboptimal under realistic coverage; ITP achieves optimal regret with monotone (non-degrading) scaling.
papers.headroom_evidence: Fig.1: BoN-Alignment first improves over pi_ref then DEGRADES as N grows (over-optimizes r-hat: high r-hat, lower true accuracy); InferenceTimePessimism is monotone/non-degrading. Proves naive argmax-BoN is provably suboptimal; ITP realizes near-optimal reward without the tail-driven collapse. (No single 'fraction-of-oracle' scalar reported.)
papers.failure_modes: As N grows BoN is driven by the extreme tail of r-hat where r-hat is mis-calibrated -> reward hacking. Requires choosing beta; requires a reward model (none given for speech).
papers.code_available: Not confirmed public at survey time.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: This is the general-purpose, principled label-free inference-time SELECTOR our I1 wants — but over text, with a trained scalar reward, and with a GLOBAL constraint (beta) rather than per-item abstention or supply-stratification. It invents the selection operator; it does not touch audio, omni-native signals, or supply-conditional headroom.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL-KILL (already-done) — the general pessimistic label-free selection operator over bare-model N-pools is already invented and proven optimal; our I1 novelty must move to modality/supply, not the operator. I2: no-threat — never sees audio/omni signals. I3: PARTIAL already-done — its chi^2/beta constraint IS a Goodhart/over-optimization guard, but global, not a per-item abstaining cross-task breakpoint detector. I4: no-threat on supply-strata — varies N only, never the capability-supply axis c (bare vs +context vs +retrieval).

papers.title: Too Consistent to Detect: A Study of Self-Consistent Errors in LLMs
papers.task: Error/hallucination detection over LLM free-form generations; studies errors repeated across stochastic samples.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Bare-model sampling: multiple stochastic (temperature) samples from one model per prompt; also a cross-model external verifier's hidden states. No beam/LM/retrieval.
papers.sees_audio: No. Text LLMs only.
papers.gold_at_train: Cross-model probe is a small trained classifier over external-verifier hidden states (needs labeled errors to train the probe).
papers.gold_at_test: No gold at test for the selector itself; gold used only to score detection AUROC.
papers.training_required: Detection baselines are training-free (self-consistency, confidence, verbalized, internal-state); the proposed cross-model probe requires training a light probe on an external verifier LLM's hidden states.
papers.scorer_inputs: Self-consistency across samples, token/verbalized confidence, internal states, and external-verifier hidden states. No audio.
papers.selection_operator: Consistency/confidence thresholding for the baselines; fused hidden-state cross-model probe for the proposed detector.
papers.comparators: Four families of detection methods (consistency-based, confidence/uncertainty, verbalized, internal-state) vs the cross-model probe.
papers.equal_budget: Partial — fixed sample count per method; not framed as an oracle-headroom vs budget sweep.
papers.datasets_used: Three LLM families (incl. Qwen, LLaMA) on QA/knowledge benchmarks (open-domain factual QA). Exact per-dataset numbers behind PDF; AUROC curves reported per model pair.
papers.eval_protocol: Define self-consistent errors (same wrong answer across samples); measure detector AUROC on self-consistent vs inconsistent error subsets; show all four baseline families fail on the self-consistent subset; cross-model probe recovers performance.
papers.headroom_evidence: Key qualitative laws with numbers: self-consistent-error frequency stays STABLE or INCREASES with model scale (inconsistent errors shrink with scale); 'all four types of detection methods significantly struggle to detect self-consistent errors'; cross-model probe (external-verifier hidden states) significantly raises AUROC across three families. This bounds the ceiling of any self-consistency/confidence selector.
papers.failure_modes: Self-consistency and confidence selection are structurally blind to self-consistent errors; sampling more does not help; fix requires an EXTERNAL (decorrelated) verifier, and a trained probe.
papers.code_available: Not confirmed public at survey time.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Directly characterizes the ceiling of a label-free self-consistency/confidence selector (our I1) and shows the escape is a cross-model/decorrelated verifier (our I2/W4 omni-decorrelation rationale) — but entirely on text, and the fix needs a trained probe, not a frozen audio-grounded signal.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: THREAT (already-ate-headroom) — a self-consistency/confidence I1 has a proven structural blind spot that grows with model scale; on our strong Qwen3-Omni this caps rho. I2: MIXED — threatens omni signals DERIVED from the same frozen model (they inherit the same self-consistent errors), but SUPPORTS an audio-grounded signal that is genuinely external/decorrelated. I3: SUPPORT/partial-prior — self-consistent errors are the un-abstainable case; their cross-model probe is a prior for cross-model abstention (but trained, not frozen). I4: tangential — scale-dependence of self-consistent errors is a supply-like law, but not pool-supply strata.

papers.title: Correlated Errors in Large Language Models
papers.task: Empirical study of error correlation across many LLMs; downstream LLM-as-judge evaluation and algorithmic-monoculture (hiring/resume-screening).
papers.candidate_source_supply: N/A to a single pool — compares INDEPENDENT models' errors on shared benchmarks (cross-model, cross-provider). Relevant as the cross-verifier supply lens.
papers.sees_audio: No. Text LLMs/leaderboards.
papers.gold_at_train: N/A (observational study using benchmark gold to label errors).
papers.gold_at_test: Uses benchmark gold to define errors; the downstream monoculture analysis is label-conditioned.
papers.training_required: None (analysis paper).
papers.scorer_inputs: Model answers + gold labels to compute pairwise error agreement.
papers.selection_operator: N/A — studies whether ensembling/second-verifier diversity actually decorrelates errors.
papers.comparators: Cross-model / cross-provider / cross-architecture pairs; 350+ LLMs.
papers.equal_budget: N/A.
papers.datasets_used: Two popular leaderboard benchmarks + a resume-screening (hiring) task; over 350 LLMs.
papers.eval_protocol: Measure pairwise agreement conditional on both models being wrong; relate correlation to model accuracy/size; propagate to LLM-as-judge and monoculture outcomes.
papers.headroom_evidence: Models AGREE ~60% of the time when both err on one leaderboard dataset; larger/more-accurate models have HIGHER error correlation even across distinct architectures/providers. Implication: adding a second (strong) verifier yields far less diversity benefit than assumed — caps ensemble/cross-model selection gains.
papers.failure_modes: Diversity assumption (different arch/provider -> decorrelated errors) is false for strong models; ensemble and LLM-as-judge inherit systematic shared errors.
papers.code_available: Not confirmed public at survey time.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Quantifies the exact risk to our W4 omni-verifier decorrelation premise (achievable delta_corr): if the audio-grounded verifier is just another strong model, its errors correlate ~60% with the generator's, gutting the second-signal benefit — but measured on text leaderboards, never on audio-vs-text context-differentiated systems.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: partial-threat — single-model self-selection is the worst case of correlation. I2: THREAT (already-ate-headroom risk) — a strong omni verifier likely shares ~60% of errors with the strong generator, threatening the decorrelation that I2/W4 needs; makes delta_corr an empirical must-measure. I3: THREAT to the 'add a second verifier' arm (correlation caps diversity) but SUPPORTS abstaining when both confidently agree-wrong. I4: tangential — correlation rises with capability (a supply dimension) but not pool-supply strata.

papers.title: Reward Model Ensembles Help Mitigate Overoptimization
papers.task: Mitigating reward over-optimization in Best-of-N sampling and PPO RLHF via conservative reward ensembles.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Bare-model sampling for the BoN arm (N samples scored by an ensemble of reward models); PPO for the training arm. No retrieval/LM lattice.
papers.sees_audio: No. Text RLHF (AlpacaFarm-style).
papers.gold_at_train: A gold/proxy reward model defines ground-truth reward; the optimized reward models are trained (incl. 25% label-noise setting).
papers.gold_at_test: Over-optimization measured against a held-out gold reward model.
papers.training_required: Requires training MULTIPLE reward models (the ensemble); BoN selection itself is inference-time.
papers.scorer_inputs: Ensemble of scalar reward models; worst-case (WCO) or uncertainty-weighted (UWO) aggregate. No audio, no gold at selection time.
papers.selection_operator: Conservative BoN: pick argmax of a pessimistic ensemble objective (WCO = min over ensemble; UWO = mean minus uncertainty penalty).
papers.comparators: Single reward model BoN/PPO; ensemble-mean; +KL penalty variants.
papers.equal_budget: Yes — BoN over matched N; over-optimization curves plotted vs KL / vs N.
papers.datasets_used: AlpacaFarm-style RLHF setup extending Gao et al. 2023 scaling-laws; adds 25% label noise.
papers.eval_protocol: Plot proxy vs gold reward as optimization proceeds (KL or N); measure over-optimization gap; report performance uplift.
papers.headroom_evidence: Conservative ensemble optimization practically ELIMINATES over-optimization and improves BoN performance by UP TO 70% (with and without label noise); for PPO, ensemble+small-KL prevents over-optimization at no performance cost. Directly eats the reward-hacking headroom that a naive single-scorer selector loses.
papers.failure_modes: Needs several trained reward models (expensive); still bounded by shared reward-model errors (ties to Kim correlated-errors); tuning of penalty weight.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: The ensemble/pessimism principle is a strong methodological prior for our constraint term (matches InferenceTimePessimism and our theory's explicit-constraint requirement), but it relies on MULTIPLE TRAINED reward models and text; our verifiable rewards (WER, exact-match) are single deterministic scorers, so the 'ensemble decorrelation' lever is not directly available without building omni-native signal ensembles.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: partial-threat (already-done for the over-optimization fix, but needs trained RM ensemble — not label-free). I2: no direct threat (text RMs, no audio) but principle transfers. I3: STRONG prior (already-done) — conservative/worst-case objective + KL is the exact Goodhart-guard mechanism I3/our theory formalize; 'practically eliminates over-optimization.' I4: no-threat on supply-strata.

papers.title: Identifying and Calibrating Overconfidence in Noisy Speech Recognition
papers.task: Confidence calibration / selective flagging for ASR under noise (audio-grounded reliability).
papers.candidate_source_supply: Single greedy ASR decode with token confidences (beam/decoder posteriors), noise-augmented audio; not an N-best selection pool.
papers.sees_audio: YES — acoustic features drive the overconfidence classifier (audio-grounded signal).
papers.gold_at_train: Overconfidence classifier + selective calibrator trained on LibriTTS clean-100 with reference transcripts (gold at train).
papers.gold_at_test: No gold at test; evaluates on R-SPIN with reference only for scoring metrics.
papers.training_required: Requires training the overconfidence classifier + selective temperature scaler (not training-free).
papers.scorer_inputs: Acoustic, uncertainty, and contextual features per token; ASR token confidences. Audio-grounded.
papers.selection_operator: Not N-best selection — token-level flagging then selective temperature scaling (calibration), a localized reliability decision.
papers.comparators: Uncalibrated Whisper; global temperature scaling; other calibration baselines.
papers.equal_budget: N/A (single decode).
papers.datasets_used: Whisper-medium-en; train LibriTTS clean-100; eval R-SPIN (400 phonetically balanced sentences, SNR-swept incl. -18..-5 dB).
papers.eval_protocol: ECE, NCE, NLL, EER, WER across SNR bins; overconfidence = high-confidence wrong tokens.
papers.headroom_evidence: 10-20% of tokens wrong with confidence>0.7 at low SNR; 11.1% high-confidence-wrong tokens at -18..-5 dB. Method cuts ECE 58% (0.086 -> 0.036) and triples NCE. Shows label-free ASR confidence is badly mis-calibrated exactly in the noisy regime = our snr5 battery.
papers.failure_modes: Recalibrates rather than abstains; needs training; no N-best selection; no cross-task/Goodhart breakpoint.
papers.code_available: Not confirmed public at survey time.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Nearest audio-grounded reliability prior to our snr5 work, and evidence that a confidence-based selector (I1) will be actively misled under noise; but it is per-token CALIBRATION on a single decode, not label-free N-best SELECTION over frozen omni pools, and it is trained.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: THREAT (evidence-of-ceiling) — in our snr5 regime label-free confidence is mis-calibrated (11.1% confident-wrong tokens), predicting the low rho_greedy ~24% we measure; a confidence-ranked I1 inherits this. I2: PARTIAL already-done — uses audio-grounded (acoustic-discrepancy) features for reliability, the same signal class I2 proposes, but for calibration not selection. I3: partial-prior — token flagging is localized abstention-like (but recalibrates, no breakpoint). I4: tangential — SNR is a difficulty axis adjacent to (not identical with) capability-supply; our clean-vs-snr5 is a difficulty stratification, not a bare/+context/+retrieval supply axis.

papers.title: Adaptation with Self-Evaluation to Improve Selective Prediction in LLMs (ASPIRE)
papers.task: Selective prediction / abstention for LLM question answering.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Bare-model generations; learns a self-evaluation selection score. No retrieval/lattice.
papers.sees_audio: No. Text QA.
papers.gold_at_train: Yes — parameter-efficient tuning + self-evaluation trained with task labels.
papers.gold_at_test: No gold at test; abstention driven by learned self-eval score. Gold used only to compute risk-coverage metrics.
papers.training_required: Requires fine-tuning (parameter-efficient / soft-prompt tuning) — NOT training-free.
papers.scorer_inputs: Learned self-evaluation score over the model's own answer; no audio.
papers.selection_operator: Threshold on learned self-evaluation selection score (answer vs abstain).
papers.comparators: Perplexity/max-softmax/self-consistency selective baselines; risk-coverage curves.
papers.equal_budget: Coverage-risk framed (AUACC/AUROC), not oracle-headroom-vs-N.
papers.datasets_used: QA datasets including CoQA, TriviaQA, SQuAD; various LLM sizes.
papers.eval_protocol: Risk-coverage: AUACC (area under accuracy-coverage), AUROC of the selection score, coverage@target-accuracy.
papers.headroom_evidence: On CoQA: AUACC 91.23% -> 92.63%; AUROC 74.61% -> 80.25% over baselines. Establishes the supervised selective-QA ceiling our training-free selector is measured against.
papers.failure_modes: Requires fine-tuning per task; no audio; no cross-task or Goodhart-breakpoint; abstention is single-model self-eval (subject to self-consistent/correlated errors from Tan/Kim).
papers.code_available: Not confirmed public at survey time.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Canonical selective-prediction/abstention anchor for QA (our I3), but it is TRAINED (soft-prompt tuning) and text-only; our I3 must deliver the abstention gain label-free/training-free over frozen speech-omni pools with a cross-task Goodhart-breakpoint detector.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: no-threat to training-free framing (ASPIRE requires fine-tuning) — it is the supervised comparator, not a training-free selector. I2: no-threat (text). I3: PRIOR (partially already-done) — a working selective-prediction/abstention method (AUROC 74.6->80.3), but trained, single-model, no breakpoint detection; leaves the training-free cross-task abstaining selector open. I4: no-threat.

papers.title: Variation in Verification: Understanding Verification Dynamics in Large Language Models
papers.task: When do verifiers help vs hurt selection over generated candidates; verifier TPR/TNR as a function of problem difficulty and generator/verifier capability.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Bare-model sampling: generator produces candidate solutions; a separate verifier scores them (best-of-N / generate-then-verify). No retrieval/lattice.
papers.sees_audio: No. Text reasoning/knowledge tasks.
papers.gold_at_train: None for the study; generative/discriminative verifiers used off-the-shelf.
papers.gold_at_test: Gold used only to compute TPR/TNR and selection accuracy; selection itself is verifier-driven.
papers.training_required: Training-free analysis (uses existing models as verifiers).
papers.scorer_inputs: Verifier judgments (correct/incorrect) over candidate solutions; no audio.
papers.selection_operator: Verifier-based selection / best-of-N with a verifier; studies TPR (recognize correct) and TNR (reject wrong).
papers.comparators: 14 models (2B-72B) + GPT-4o as generators and verifiers, crossed by difficulty.
papers.equal_budget: Yes — fixed-verifier comparisons across generator strengths; scaling analyzed.
papers.datasets_used: 4,244 problems: 2,347 math (GSM8K, MATH500, OlympiadBench, AIME, AMC, Minerva), 1,196 knowledge (MMLU-Pro, GPQA), 901 NL reasoning (BBEH, ReClor, FOLIO).
papers.eval_protocol: Decompose selection into TPR (by difficulty) and TNR (by generator strength); linear/saturation/threshold regimes by verifier capability.
papers.headroom_evidence: Verifier TNR DROPS from 0.68 on weak-generator (Llama-3.1-8B) errors to 0.17 on strong-generator (Qwen3-32B) errors — strong generators' errors are nearly undetectable. A fixed verifier lets weak Gemma2-9B close 75.5% of the gap to Gemma2-27B (10.3%->2.5%). 'Verifier scaling alone cannot overcome fundamental verification challenges' on hard problems/strong generators.
papers.failure_modes: Verification gain collapses for strong generators and hard problems; verifier scaling has diminishing/threshold returns.
papers.code_available: Not confirmed public at survey time.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: Most direct predictor of our realized-headroom ceiling: our generator (Qwen3-Omni-30B) is a STRONG generator, so a verifier's TNR on its errors is low (~0.17 analog) -> low rho, matching our measured rho_greedy ~24% (snr5). It also stratifies by difficulty/generator size — the closest existing analog to our I4 supply-stratification — but never by capability SUPPLY (bare vs +context vs +retrieval), and never on audio.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: THREAT (already-ate/bounds-headroom) — realized selection gain is capped by generator strength; on strong Qwen3-Omni, TNR~0.17-analog predicts low rho, structurally limiting a label-free N-best selector. I2: THREAT — audio-grounded verifier still faces low TNR on a strong generator's errors unless audio supplies genuinely new info. I3: SUPPORT — verification collapses on hard items -> abstain there (motivates I3's breakpoint). I4: PARTIAL-PRIOR/partial-threat — stratifies verification by difficulty and generator capability (a supply-like axis) but NOT by bare/+context/+retrieval supply; leaves I4's supply-conditional H(c) open.

killtest_datasets: librispeech (test-other + snr5): direct kill test for ASR selective-prediction/overconfidence (paper 5) and for pessimistic/verifier selection (papers 1,7) using WER as verifiable reward at N=8 — our measured rho_greedy 24% (snr5)/42% (clean) and oracle headroom +0.042 CI[0.029,0.056] are already the equal-K substrate

aime24/25/26: direct text-reasoning kill test matching papers 1,2,3,7 (GSM8K/MATH/AIME analogs) — exact-match reward, measure self-consistent-error fraction (Tan), verifier TNR on strong-generator errors (Variation in Verification), pessimistic-BoN vs oracle (InferenceTimePessimism)
spoken-squad and heysquad: spoken-QA selective-prediction/self-consistency kill test (papers 2,6,7) with exact-match reward

mmau-mini, mmsu, big-bench-audio: multiple-choice audio-understanding, gradeable — kill test for self-consistent/correlated errors and verification-dynamics (papers 2,3,7) with strong Qwen3-Omni generator
slurp, minds14: intent/SLU exact-match — selective-prediction/abstention comparator (papers 1,6)
covost2, fleurs-r: ST with WER-style reward — secondary ASR selective-prediction comparator (paper 5)
families.saturation_note: This family is MATURE on text-LLM reasoning/RLHF and on ASR calibration: the core mechanisms are already invented and proven — pessimistic/chi^2-constrained inference-time selection (InferenceTimePessimism, ICML 2025), conservative reward-model ensembles that eliminate over-optimization and lift BoN up to 70% (Coste, ICLR 2024), selective-prediction/abstention with risk-coverage metrics (ASPIRE, AUROC 74.6->80.3), and hard limits on verification: self-consistent errors defeat all label-free consistency/confidence selectors and grow with scale (Tan, EMNLP 2025), strong models' errors correlate ~60% across providers (Kim, ICML 2025), and verifier TNR collapses from 0.68 to 0.17 as the generator gets stronger (Variation in Verification, 2025). The strongest KILL pressure is convergent and structural: because our frozen Qwen3-Omni-30B is a STRONG generator, self-consistent + correlated + hard-to-verify errors jointly predict a LOW realized-headroom ceiling for any naive label-free selector — consistent with our own measured rho_greedy ~24% (snr5). The selection OPERATOR itself (pessimistic/label-free N-best) is therefore near-saturated and NOT a defensible novelty. What remains genuinely UN-saturated and is exactly where our identity must live: (a) audio-grounded/omni-native signals that supply information DECORRELATED from a strong text generator (the only documented escape from the self-consistent/correlated-error ceiling — but decorrelation-achievability, our delta_corr, is unmeasured for audio-vs-text); and (b) SUPPLY-stratified headroom H(c) across bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval — no paper in this family varies the capability-supply axis (the closest, Variation in Verification, stratifies only by problem difficulty and generator size).
gaps: Supply-stratification (I4) is untouched: no paper varies capability-supply c (bare-core vs +context vs +retrieval); the closest work (Variation in Verification) stratifies verification only by problem difficulty and generator/verifier size, and reports no oracle-headroom-as-a-function-of-supply curve.

No audio/omni-native operation: the entire multi-verifier/pessimism literature is text-LLM; ASR work (paper 5) is single-decode token CALIBRATION/flagging, never label-free N-best SELECTION over frozen omni pools with audio-grounded signals.

Equal-K vs oracle-headroom rarely reported as a realization fraction (rho): papers report win-rate, AUROC, or over-optimization gap, not 'fraction of best-of-N oracle headroom realized at matched N' — our rho_greedy framing is not a standard reported quantity in this family.

Training-free is the exception, not the rule: the strongest methods need a trained reward model (InferenceTimePessimism, Coste) or fine-tuning (ASPIRE); genuinely label-free/training-free selection over verifiable rewards (WER/exact-match) is under-explored as its own method.

Decorrelation-achievability (our delta_corr / W4 omni bridge) is asserted-needed but unmeasured for audio-vs-text: Kim shows strong cross-model verifiers correlate ~60% on errors and Tan shows same-model signals are blind to self-consistent errors, yet no work measures whether an audio-grounded verifier is actually decorrelated from a strong omni generator.

No explicit per-item Goodhart-breakpoint DETECTOR feeding a cross-task abstention decision: InferenceTimePessimism/Coste use a GLOBAL constraint (beta / worst-case ensemble); ASPIRE abstains per-item but single-task and trained; nobody exposes a supply-conditional over-optimization breakpoint as an abstain signal across ASR/ST/SER/SLU/QA/audio-understanding tasks.

families.family: Reference-free ASR quality estimation / WER estimation (NoRefER lineage)

papers.title: Word Error Rate Estimation for Speech Recognition: e-WER (original)
papers.task: Estimate the WER of a SINGLE ASR system's output on unlabeled test audio without a gold transcript; feed-forward net predicts #errors and word count per utterance, aggregated to corpus WER.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Single-ASR-system output only (glass-box = internal decoder/lattice features; black-box = ASR text + numeral/character recognition). No per-utterance candidate pool, no sampling, no beam N-best used for selection.
papers.sees_audio: Partial — uses decoder/acoustic-derived features (durations, posteriors, phone-level), not raw-waveform or omni embeddings. Black-box variant is text-only.
papers.gold_at_train: Yes — regressor trained on reference-labeled utterances (error counts).
papers.gold_at_test: No — that is the contribution (no gold transcript at test).
papers.training_required: Yes — supervised feed-forward regressor.
papers.scorer_inputs: ASR recognized text + character-recognition results + internal decoder features (glass-box) or text-only features (black-box).
papers.selection_operator: None — scalar WER/error-count regression. Does NOT choose among candidate hypotheses.
papers.comparators: Glass-box vs black-box variants; compared against actual/reference WER.
papers.equal_budget: N/A — single-output estimation, no K-budget notion.
papers.datasets_used: 24 Arabic broadcast programs (MGB-style), ~3h / 1,400 sentences test.
papers.eval_protocol: Corpus-level estimated WER vs actual WER; per-sentence RMSE.
papers.headroom_evidence: No N-best headroom concept. Estimated overall e-WER 25.3% vs actual 28.5% on the 3h set; 16.9% WER RMSE across 1,400 sentences.
papers.failure_modes: Systematic under/over-estimation of corpus WER; per-sentence error high; Arabic-broadcast-only, single-domain.
papers.code_available: Yes — github.com/qcri/e-wer (reference implementation of the e-WER lineage).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: It ESTIMATES a scalar WER for one output; we SELECT the best of K frozen-omni samples and measure oracle-headroom realization. It never touches the selection/headroom axis at all.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: no-threat (estimates single-system WER, never selects among N, realizes 0 headroom). I2: no-threat (decoder-feature/text estimation, not audio-grounded selection). I3: no-threat (ASR-only, no abstention/Goodhart). I4: no-threat (no supply stratification).

papers.title: Word Error Rate Estimation Without ASR Output: e-WER2
papers.task: Multistream end-to-end WER estimation of a single system, extended to a 'no-box' regime that estimates WER WITHOUT any ASR output — from phoneme-recognition + MFCC acoustics only.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Single system; the no-box variant does not even use ASR hypotheses (phoneme recognizer + MFCC). No candidate pool / no N-best selection.
papers.sees_audio: Yes for no-box (MFCC acoustic + phoneme-recognition joint acoustic-lexical repr.); glass/black-box partial.
papers.gold_at_train: Yes — supervised on reference error labels.
papers.training_required: Yes — multistream neural estimator.
papers.scorer_inputs: Acoustic (MFCC), phonotactic (phoneme recognition), and lexical features; decoder features for glass-box.
papers.selection_operator: None — scalar WER regression, no hypothesis choice.
papers.comparators: e-WER (2018); glass-box vs black-box vs no-box variants.
papers.equal_budget: N/A.
papers.datasets_used: Arabic broadcast, 1,400 sentences / ~3h test.
papers.eval_protocol: Pearson correlation + RMSE per-sentence; corpus estimated vs actual WER.
papers.headroom_evidence: No selection/headroom. No-box: Pearson 0.56, RMSE 0.24 across 1,400 sentences; estimated WER 30.9% vs reference 28.5%.
papers.failure_modes: Modest per-sentence correlation (0.56); no-box weakest; single-language/domain.
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: The no-box 'estimate quality from audio alone' idea is conceptually adjacent to I2's audio-grounding, but it outputs a scalar WER (0.56 PCC), never ranks/selects K candidates and never realizes headroom.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: no-threat (estimation only, no selection). I2: partial-relevance/no-threat (audio-only quality estimate, PCC 0.56, but does not select among candidates, does not realize headroom). I3: no-threat (ASR-only, no abstention). I4: no-threat (no supply stratification).

papers.title: NoRefER: a Referenceless Quality Metric for ASR via Semi-Supervised LM Fine-Tuning with Contrastive Learning
papers.task: Referenceless quality metric that PAIR-WISE RANKS ASR hypotheses (Siamese/contrastive XLM-R); learns intra-sample quality order and (semi-sup) inter-sample WER scale.
papers.candidate_source_supply: Training pairs from 6 Whisper compression levels (800,340 self-sup pairs) + outputs of 6 commercial engines (AWS/Azure/Google/Deepgram/AppTek/Whisper). Supply = engine/compression-level variants, NOT per-utterance sampling or beam N-best.
papers.sees_audio: No — text-only (operates on hypothesis transcriptions).
papers.gold_at_train: Yes for semi-sup (referenced dataset for inter-sample ranking); self-sup uses WER-ordered compression levels (labels derived from references).
papers.training_required: Yes — contrastive fine-tuning of XLM-RoBERTa (Siamese). NOT training-free.
papers.scorer_inputs: Pairs of hypothesis transcripts; sigmoid on logit difference gives pairwise preference.
papers.selection_operator: Pairwise sigmoid ranking -> argmax = intra-sample hypothesis SELECTION (selection-capable; the family's first genuine reference-free ranker).
papers.comparators: XLM-RoBERTa-Large perplexity (Pearson 0.20-0.29 ranking); commercial-engine WER ranks.
papers.equal_budget: No equal-K framing; ranks whatever hypotheses are supplied. Reports correlation, not WER-after-selection.
papers.datasets_used: Train: CMU-MOSEI+MOSEAS (134h, multilingual), Common Voice (148,393 hyps). Test: Common Voice (en/fr/es), LibriSpeech-clean, proprietary non-native meetings.
papers.eval_protocol: Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlation of metric vs WER ranks and WER scores (intra- and inter-sample).
papers.headroom_evidence: No WER-after-selection / headroom-realization reported. Pearson RANKING corr: CV-en 0.56(self)/0.53(semi), CV-fr 0.48/0.48, CV-es 0.58/0.56, LibriSpeech-clean 0.42/0.57, non-native 0.37/0.38. Score corr 0.10-0.53. vs XLM-R perplexity 0.20-0.29.
papers.failure_modes: Text-only -> blind to acoustics; self-sup weak on inter-sample (score) corr; semi-sup depends on reference data; correlations modest (0.4-0.6) and drop on non-native (0.37).
papers.closest_delta_to_ours: NoRefER is the strongest TEXT-ONLY reference-free N-best ranker and the concept nearest I1, but (a) it is trained (contrastive), not training-free; (b) text-only, so no audio grounding (I2); (c) reports correlation only, never headroom realized; (d) never applied to omni-MLLM K-pools or supply-stratified.
papers.kill_relevance: I1: PARTIAL-THREAT (does label-free N-best ranking; Pearson 0.42-0.58) but requires supervised contrastive training and reports no headroom-realization -> does not close the training-free/headroom gap. I2: no-threat (text-only, no audio). I3: no-threat (single ASR task, no abstention/Goodhart). I4: no-threat (compression-level supply, no capability-supply-stratified headroom).

papers.gold_at_train: Yes — supervised regression to true WER.
papers.training_required: Yes — supervised estimator (BiLSTM + regressor).
papers.scorer_inputs: Avg-pooled XLSR-53 speech repr (BiLSTM concat both directions) + avg-pooled XLM-R transcript repr.
papers.selection_operator: None — scalar WER regression.
papers.comparators: Prior WER-estimator baseline (e-WER lineage).

papers.datasets_used: TED-LIUM 3.
papers.eval_protocol: Pearson correlation + RMSE vs true WER; real-time-factor for speed.

papers.sees_audio: Yes — two-tower HuBERT-large speech + XLM-R text, 1024-d each, concatenated to MLP.
papers.gold_at_train: Yes — references used to synthesize erroneous hypotheses and as regression targets.
papers.gold_at_test: No — estimates WER of a given (audio, hypothesis) pair without reference.
papers.training_required: Yes — supervised MLP on two-tower features.
papers.scorer_inputs: Frame-level HuBERT speech features (avg) + token-level XLM-R text features (avg), concatenated.
papers.selection_operator: None — scalar WER regression per (audio, hypothesis). No hypothesis selection.
papers.comparators: Fe-WER (Park 2023), e-WER2 (2020), e-WER3 (Chowdhury&Ali 2023); 5 ASR configs.
papers.equal_budget: N/A.
papers.datasets_used: Train: TED-LIUM3 (444.62h synth). Eval in-domain: TL3 test; OOD: AMI, Switchboard/CALLHOME, WSJ.

papers.selection_operator: None — approximates a scalar metric per system/utterance; does NOT rank/select among per-utterance candidates.
papers.comparators: 'Most recent baseline' (>50% relative improvement over it); true WER/CER as ground truth.

papers.gold_at_test: YES — REFERENCE-BASED (requires gold transcription at test). Not reference-free.

papers.gold_at_train: No — no training tailored to ASR model/dataset.

papers.selection_operator: argmin acoustic-discrepancy over the top-5 candidates -> true N-best hypothesis SELECTION.
papers.comparators: Oracle best-of-N (upper bound) and top-1 baseline. NO comparison vs NoRefER or LM rescoring (a gap).
papers.equal_budget: Fixed top-5 pool; not framed as equal-K sweep vs alternative selectors.

Relative WER -2.9% to -21.5%; realizes only ~14% of oracle headroom on LS-clean, ~a third on SWBD -> LARGE residual headroom left.
